content: Therein, what is the eye faculty? The eye that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements… this is an empty village – this is called "the eye faculty". ⤵ Therein, what is the ear faculty… the nose faculty… the tongue faculty… the body faculty? The body that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements… this is an empty village – this is called "the body faculty". ⤵ Therein, what is the mind faculty? As a single class, the mind faculty is joined with contact. As a twofold class: there is mind with a root cause, and mind without a root cause. As a threefold class: there is wholesome mind, unwholesome mind, and neutral mind. As a fourfold class: there is mind belonging to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, and mind not included in any sphere. As a fivefold class: there is mind joined with the faculty of pleasure, joined with the faculty of pain, joined with the faculty of gladness, joined with the faculty of sadness, and joined with the faculty of equanimity. As a sixfold class: there is eye-consciousness… mind-consciousness. This is the mind faculty as a sixfold class. ⤵ As a sevenfold class: there is eye-consciousness… body-consciousness, the mind element, and the mind-consciousness element. This is the mind faculty as a sevenfold class. ⤵ As an eightfold class: there is eye-consciousness… body-consciousness – which may be accompanied by pleasure or by pain – the mind element, and the mind-consciousness element. This is the mind faculty as an eightfold class. ⤵ As a ninefold class: there is eye-consciousness… body-consciousness, the mind element, and the mind-consciousness element – which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is the mind faculty as a ninefold class. ⤵ As a tenfold class: there is eye-consciousness… body-consciousness – which may be accompanied by pleasure or by pain – the mind element, and the mind-consciousness element – which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is the mind faculty as a tenfold class… thus the mind faculty is classified in many ways. This is called "the mind faculty". ⤵ Therein, what is the faculty of femininity? A woman's feminine features, feminine marks, feminine ways, feminine manner, femininity, the state of being a woman – this is called "the faculty of femininity". ⤵ Therein, what is the faculty of masculinity? A man's masculine features, masculine marks, masculine ways, masculine manner, masculinity, the state of being a man – this is called "the faculty of masculinity". ⤵ Therein, what is the life faculty? The life faculty is twofold: there is the material life faculty, and there is the immaterial life faculty. ⤵ Therein, what is the material life faculty? The life span of material states, their persistence, their keeping going, their being kept going, their continuing, their proceeding, their maintenance, their life, the life faculty – this is called "the material life faculty". ⤵ Therein, what is the immaterial life faculty? The life span of immaterial states, their persistence, their keeping going, their being kept going, their continuing, their proceeding, their maintenance, their life, the life faculty – this is called "the immaterial life faculty". This is called "the life faculty". ⤵ Therein, what is the faculty of pleasure? Bodily comfort, bodily pleasure; the comfortable, pleasant experience born of body-contact; the comfortable, pleasant feeling born of body-contact – this is called "the faculty of pleasure". ⤵ Therein, what is the faculty of pain? Bodily discomfort, bodily pain; the uncomfortable, painful experience born of body-contact; the uncomfortable, painful feeling born of body-contact – this is called "the faculty of pain". ⤵ Therein, what is the faculty of gladness? Mental comfort, mental pleasure; the comfortable, pleasant experience born of mind-contact; the comfortable, pleasant feeling born of mind-contact – this is called "the faculty of gladness". ⤵ Therein, what is the faculty of sadness? Mental discomfort, mental pain; the uncomfortable, painful experience born of mind-contact; the uncomfortable, painful feeling born of mind-contact – this is called "the faculty of sadness". ⤵ Therein, what is the faculty of equanimity? What is mentally neither comfortable nor uncomfortable; the experience born of mind-contact that is neither painful nor pleasant; the feeling born of mind-contact that is neither painful nor pleasant – this is called "the faculty of equanimity". ⤵ Therein, what is the faculty of confidence? The confidence, the trusting, the reliance, the deep trust; confidence, the faculty of confidence, the power of confidence – this is called "the faculty of confidence". ⤵ Therein, what is the faculty of energy? The mental arousing of energy, the exertion, the endeavour, the striving, the effort, the zeal, the persistence, the vigour, the steadiness, the unslackening endeavour, the not putting down of desire, the not putting down of the burden, the firm taking up of the burden; energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy – this is called "the faculty of energy". ⤵ Therein, what is the faculty of mindfulness? The mindfulness, the remembering, the recollecting; mindfulness, the bearing in mind, the keeping in mind, the non-drifting, the non-forgetting; mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness – this is called "the faculty of mindfulness". ⤵ Therein, what is the faculty of concentration? The steadiness of mind, the stability, the standing firm, the non-scattering, the non-distraction, the undistracted state of mind; calm, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, right concentration – this is called "the faculty of concentration". ⤵ Therein, what is the faculty of wisdom? The wisdom, the understanding… the non-delusion, the investigation of states, right view – this is called "the faculty of wisdom". ⤵ Therein, what is the faculty of "I shall know what is not yet known"? The wisdom, the understanding… the non-delusion, the investigation of states, the right view, the awakening factor of investigation of states that is a path factor, included in the path, for the realizing of those states not yet known, not yet seen, not yet reached, not yet found, not yet realized – this is called "the faculty of 'I shall know what is not yet known'". ⤵ Therein, what is the faculty of final knowledge? The wisdom, the understanding… the non-delusion, the investigation of states, the right view, the awakening factor of investigation of states that is a path factor, included in the path, for the realizing of those states that are known, seen, reached, found, and realized – this is called the faculty of final knowledge. ⤵ Therein, what is the faculty of one who has fully known? The wisdom, the understanding… the non-delusion, the investigation of states, the right view, the awakening factor of investigation of states that is a path factor, included in the path, of one who has fully known those states that are seen, reached, found, and realized – this is called "the faculty of one who has fully known".
The Classification According to the Abhidhamma is finished.

Therein, what is the faculty of equanimity? What is mentally neither comfortable nor uncomfortable; the experience born of mind-contact that is neither painful nor pleasant; the feeling born of mind-contact that is neither painful nor pleasant – this is called "the faculty of equanimity".
Therein, what is the faculty of confidence? The confidence, the trusting, the reliance, the deep trust; confidence, the faculty of confidence, the power of confidence – this is called "the faculty of confidence".
Therein, what is the faculty of energy? The mental arousing of energy, the exertion, the endeavour, the striving, the effort, the zeal, the persistence, the vigour, the steadiness, the unslackening endeavour, the not putting down of desire, the not putting down of the burden, the firm taking up of the burden; energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy – this is called "the faculty of energy".
Therein, what is the faculty of mindfulness? The mindfulness, the remembering, the recollecting; mindfulness, the bearing in mind, the keeping in mind, the non-drifting, the non-forgetting; mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness – this is called "the faculty of mindfulness".
Therein, what is the faculty of concentration? The steadiness of mind, the stability, the standing firm, the non-scattering, the non-distraction, the undistracted state of mind; calm, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, right concentration – this is called "the faculty of concentration".
Therein, what is the faculty of wisdom? The wisdom, the understanding… the non-delusion, the investigation of states, right view – this is called "the faculty of wisdom".
Therein, what is the faculty of "I shall know what is not yet known"? The wisdom, the understanding… the non-delusion, the investigation of states, the right view, the awakening factor of investigation of states that is a path factor, included in the path, for the realizing of those states not yet known, not yet seen, not yet reached, not yet found, not yet realized – this is called "the faculty of 'I shall know what is not yet known'".
Therein, what is the faculty of final knowledge? The wisdom, the understanding… the non-delusion, the investigation of states, the right view, the awakening factor of investigation of states that is a path factor, included in the path, for the realizing of those states that are known, seen, reached, found, and realized – this is called the faculty of final knowledge.
Therein, what is the faculty of one who has fully known? The wisdom, the understanding… the non-delusion, the investigation of states, the right view, the awakening factor of investigation of states that is a path factor, included in the path, of one who has fully known those states that are seen, reached, found, and realized – this is called "the faculty of one who has fully known".
The Classification According to the Abhidhamma is finished.

content: Therein, what is ignorance? The lack of knowledge, lack of vision… the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root — this is called "ignorance". ⤵ Therein, what is the formation that has ignorance as condition? The intention, intending, state of intending — this is called "the formation that has ignorance as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the consciousness that has the formation as condition? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the consciousness that has the formation as condition". ⤵ Therein, what are the mentality and material form that have consciousness as condition? There is mentality, there is material form. Therein, what is mentality? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations — this is called "mentality". Therein, what is material form? The growth of the eye sense-field, the growth of the ear sense-field, the growth of the nose sense-field, the growth of the tongue sense-field, the growth of the body sense-field, or whatever other material form there is that is born of mind, caused by mind, originated by mind — this is called "material form". So this is mentality and this is material form. This is called "the mentality and material form that have consciousness as condition". ⤵ "With mentality and material form as condition, the six sense-fields": there is mentality, there is material form. Therein, what is mentality? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations — this is called "mentality". Therein, what is material form? The four great elements and the material form depending on which the mind-consciousness element occurs — this is called "material form". So this is mentality and this is material form. This is called "mentality and material form". ⤵ Therein, what are the six sense-fields that have mentality and material form as condition? The eye sense-field, the ear sense-field, the nose sense-field, the tongue sense-field, the body sense-field, the mind sense-field — this is called "the six sense-fields that have mentality and material form as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the contact that has the sixth sense-field as condition? The contact, touching, being in contact, state of being in contact — this is called "the contact that has the sixth sense-field as condition"… therefore it is said, "thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering".
The Tetrad of Conditions.

"Thus there is the origin of these things": thus there is the coming together of these things, their meeting, their combination, their appearance. Therefore it is said, "thus there is the origin of these things".
The Exposition of the Wholesome.

content: Which things are neutral? On the occasion when one develops an immaterial-sphere meditative absorption — functional, neither wholesome nor unwholesome and not the result of action, a pleasant dwelling in this very life — completely passing beyond the field of nothingness, accompanied by the perception of the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, with the abandoning of happiness… one enters and dwells in the fourth meditative absorption — on that occasion, with the formation as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, mentality; with mentality as condition, the sixth sense-field; with the sixth sense-field as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, confidence; with confidence as condition, decision; with decision as condition, existence; with existence as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging and death. Thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.
The Exposition of the Neutral.

The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the consciousness that has the formation as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the mentality that has consciousness as condition? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations — this is called "the mentality that has consciousness as condition". ⤵ Therein, what is the sixth sense-field that has mentality as condition? Therefore it is said, "thus there is the origin of this entire mass of suffering".

Classification According to the Discourses

There are four foundations of mindfulness. Here a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body internally, dwells contemplating the body in the body externally, dwells contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings internally, dwells contemplating feelings in feelings externally, dwells contemplating feelings in feelings both internally and externally — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world. He dwells contemplating the mind in the mind internally, dwells contemplating the mind in the mind externally, dwells contemplating the mind in the mind both internally and externally — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world. He dwells contemplating mental objects in mental objects internally, dwells contemplating mental objects in mental objects externally, dwells contemplating mental objects in mental objects both internally and externally — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world.
The Exposition of Contemplating the Body

And how does a monk dwell contemplating the body in the body internally? Here a monk reviews his own body internally, from the soles of the feet up and from the top of the head down, enclosed by skin, full of many kinds of impurity: "There are in this body head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, membranes, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, stomach contents, excrement, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, fluid of the joints, urine." He practises that sign, develops it, cultivates it, and establishes it well. Having practised that sign, developed it, cultivated it, and established it well, he directs his mind to the body externally.
And how does a monk dwell contemplating the body in the body externally? Here a monk reviews a body externally, from the soles of the feet up and from the top of the head down, enclosed by skin, full of many kinds of impurity: "There are in this person's body head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, membranes, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, stomach contents, excrement, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, fluid of the joints, urine." He practises that sign, develops it, cultivates it, and establishes it well. Having practised that sign, developed it, cultivated it, and established it well, he directs his mind to the body both internally and externally.
And how does a monk dwell contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally? Here a monk reviews the body both internally and externally, from the soles of the feet up and from the top of the head down, enclosed by skin, full of many kinds of impurity: "There are in this body head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, membranes, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, stomach contents, excrement, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, fluid of the joints, urine." Thus a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world.

"Contemplating": therein, what is contemplation? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view — this is called "contemplation". He is endowed with this contemplation, fully endowed, having reached it, fully reached it, possessed of it, complete in it, furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "contemplating".
"Dwells": he moves, goes on, keeps going, maintains himself, carries on, conducts himself, dwells. Therefore it is said, "dwells".

"Ardent": therein, what is ardour? The mental initiation of energy… right effort — this is called "ardour". He is endowed with this ardour, fully endowed, having reached it, fully reached it, possessed of it, complete in it, furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "ardent".

"Clearly comprehending": therein, what is clear comprehension? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view — this is called "clear comprehension". He is endowed with this clear comprehension, fully endowed, having reached it, fully reached it, possessed of it, complete in it, furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "clearly comprehending".

"Mindful": therein, what is mindfulness? The mindfulness, recollection… right mindfulness — this is called "mindfulness". He is endowed with this mindfulness, fully endowed, having reached it, fully reached it, possessed of it, complete in it, furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "mindful".

"Having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world": therein, what is the world? This very body is the world; the five aggregates that can be clung to are also the world. This is called "the world". Therein, what is covetousness? The lust, passion… passion of the mind — this is called "covetousness". Therein, what is grief? Mental discomfort, mental pain, the uncomfortable painful experience born of mind-contact, the uncomfortable painful feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "grief". So this covetousness and this grief are removed in this world, thoroughly removed, stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world".
The Exposition of Contemplating the Body.
The Exposition of Contemplating Feelings

And how does a monk dwell contemplating feelings in feelings internally? Here a monk, feeling a pleasant feeling, knows "I feel a pleasant feeling"; feeling a painful feeling, he knows "I feel a painful feeling"; feeling a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he knows "I feel a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling"; feeling a worldly pleasant feeling, he knows "I feel a worldly pleasant feeling"; feeling an unworldly pleasant feeling, he knows "I feel an unworldly pleasant feeling"; feeling a worldly painful feeling, he knows "I feel a worldly painful feeling"; feeling an unworldly painful feeling, he knows "I feel an unworldly painful feeling"; feeling a worldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he knows "I feel a worldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling"; feeling an unworldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he knows "I feel an unworldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling". He practises that sign, develops it, cultivates it, and establishes it well. Having practised that sign, developed it, cultivated it, and established it well, he directs his mind to feelings externally.
And how does a monk dwell contemplating feelings in feelings externally? Here a monk knows of one feeling a pleasant feeling, "he feels a pleasant feeling"; of one feeling a painful feeling, he knows "he feels a painful feeling"; of one feeling a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he knows "he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling"; of one feeling a worldly pleasant feeling, he knows "he feels a worldly pleasant feeling"; of one feeling an unworldly pleasant feeling, he knows "he feels an unworldly pleasant feeling"; of one feeling a worldly painful feeling, he knows "he feels a worldly painful feeling"; of one feeling an unworldly painful feeling, he knows "he feels an unworldly painful feeling"; of one feeling a worldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he knows "he feels a worldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling"; of one feeling an unworldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he knows "he feels an unworldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling". He practises that sign, develops it, cultivates it, and establishes it well. Having practised that sign, developed it, cultivated it, and established it well, he directs his mind to feelings both internally and externally.
And how does a monk dwell contemplating feelings in feelings both internally and externally? Here a monk knows a pleasant feeling as "a pleasant feeling"; he knows a painful feeling as "a painful feeling"; he knows a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling as "a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling"; he knows a worldly pleasant feeling as "a worldly pleasant feeling"; he knows an unworldly pleasant feeling as "an unworldly pleasant feeling"; he knows a worldly painful feeling as "a worldly painful feeling"; he knows an unworldly painful feeling as "an unworldly painful feeling"; he knows a worldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling as "a worldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling"; he knows an unworldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling as "an unworldly neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling". Thus a monk dwells contemplating feelings in feelings both internally and externally — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world.

"Contemplating"… "dwells"… "ardent"… "clearly comprehending"… "mindful"… "having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world": therein, what is the world? That very feeling is the world; the five aggregates that can be clung to are also the world. This is called "the world". Therein, what is covetousness? The lust, passion… passion of the mind — this is called "covetousness". Therein, what is grief? Mental discomfort, mental pain, the uncomfortable painful experience born of mind-contact, the uncomfortable painful feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "grief". So this covetousness and this grief are removed in this world, thoroughly removed, stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world".
The Exposition of Contemplating Feelings.
The Exposition of Contemplating the Mind

And how does a monk dwell contemplating the mind in the mind internally? Here a monk knows a mind with lust as "my mind has lust"; he knows a mind without lust as "my mind is without lust"; he knows a mind with hate as "my mind has hate"; he knows a mind without hate as "my mind is without hate"; he knows a mind with delusion as "my mind has delusion"; he knows a mind without delusion as "my mind is without delusion"; he knows a contracted mind as "my mind is contracted"; he knows a distracted mind as "my mind is distracted"; he knows an expanded mind as "my mind is expanded"; he knows an unexpanded mind as "my mind is unexpanded"; he knows a surpassable mind as "my mind is surpassable"; he knows an unsurpassable mind as "my mind is unsurpassable"; he knows a concentrated mind as "my mind is concentrated"; he knows an unconcentrated mind as "my mind is unconcentrated"; he knows a freed mind as "my mind is freed"; he knows an unfreed mind as "my mind is unfreed". He practises that sign, develops it, cultivates it, and establishes it well. Having practised that sign, developed it, cultivated it, and established it well, he directs his mind to the mind externally.
And how does a monk dwell contemplating the mind in the mind externally? Here a monk knows another's mind with lust as "his mind has lust"; he knows his mind without lust as "his mind is without lust"; he knows his mind with hate as "his mind has hate"; he knows his mind without hate as "his mind is without hate"; he knows his mind with delusion as "his mind has delusion"; he knows his mind without delusion as "his mind is without delusion"; he knows his contracted mind as "his mind is contracted"; he knows his distracted mind as "his mind is distracted"; he knows his expanded mind as "his mind is expanded"; he knows his unexpanded mind as "his mind is unexpanded"; he knows his surpassable mind as "his mind is surpassable"; he knows his unsurpassable mind as "his mind is unsurpassable"; he knows his concentrated mind as "his mind is concentrated"; he knows his unconcentrated mind as "his mind is unconcentrated"; he knows his freed mind as "his mind is freed"; he knows his unfreed mind as "his mind is unfreed". He practises that sign, develops it, cultivates it, and establishes it well. Having practised that sign, developed it, cultivated it, and established it well, he directs his mind to the mind both internally and externally.
And how does a monk dwell contemplating the mind in the mind both internally and externally? Here a monk knows a mind with lust as "a mind with lust"; he knows a mind without lust as "a mind without lust"; he knows a mind with hate as "a mind with hate"; he knows a mind without hate as "a mind without hate"; he knows a mind with delusion as "a mind with delusion"; he knows a mind without delusion as "a mind without delusion"; he knows a contracted mind as "a contracted mind"; he knows a distracted mind as "a distracted mind"; he knows an expanded mind as "an expanded mind"; he knows an unexpanded mind as "an unexpanded mind"; he knows a surpassable mind as "a surpassable mind"; he knows an unsurpassable mind as "an unsurpassable mind"; he knows a concentrated mind as "a concentrated mind"; he knows an unconcentrated mind as "an unconcentrated mind"; he knows a freed mind as "a freed mind"; he knows an unfreed mind as "an unfreed mind". Thus a monk dwells contemplating the mind in the mind both internally and externally — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world.

"Contemplating"… "dwells"… "ardent"… "clearly comprehending"… "mindful"… "having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world": therein, what is the world? The Exposition of Contemplating the Mind.
The Exposition of Contemplating Mental Objects

And how does a monk dwell contemplating mental objects in mental objects internally? Here a monk, when sense desire is present in him, knows "sense desire is present in me"; when sense desire is not present in him, he knows "sense desire is not present in me"; he knows how unarisen sense desire arises; he knows how arisen sense desire is abandoned; and he knows how abandoned sense desire does not arise again in the future. When ill will is present in him… when dullness and drowsiness are present in him… when restlessness and remorse are present in him… when doubt is present in him, he knows "doubt is present in me"; when doubt is not present in him, he knows "doubt is not present in me"; he knows how unarisen doubt arises; he knows how arisen doubt is abandoned; and he knows how abandoned doubt does not arise again in the future.
When the awakening factor of mindfulness is present in him, he knows "the awakening factor of mindfulness is present in me"; when the awakening factor of mindfulness is not present in him, he knows "the awakening factor of mindfulness is not present in me"; he knows how the unarisen awakening factor of mindfulness arises; and he knows how the arisen awakening factor of mindfulness is perfected by development. He practises that sign, develops it, cultivates it, and establishes it well. So this covetousness and this grief are removed in this world, thoroughly removed, stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world".

Analysis of the Right Efforts
Classification According to the Discourses

There are four right efforts. Here a monk generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the abandoning of evil, unwholesome things that have arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the arising of wholesome things that have not yet arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the persistence of wholesome things that have arisen, for their non-confusion, their increase, their expansion, their development, their perfection.

And how does a monk generate desire, strive, initiate energy, exert his mind, and endeavour for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen? Therein, what are the evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen? The three unwholesome roots — greed, hate, delusion — and the defilements that stand together with them; the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness associated with them; and the bodily action, verbal action, and mental action originated by them — these are called "the evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen". So he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the non-arising of these evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen.

"Generates desire": therein, what is desire? The desire, wishing, wish to act, wholesome desire for the Dhamma — this is called "desire". He generates this desire, brings it forth, raises it, rouses it, produces it, brings it into being. Therefore it is said, "generates desire".

"Strives": therein, what is striving? The mental initiation of energy… right effort — this is called "striving". He is endowed with this striving, fully endowed, having reached it, fully reached it, possessed of it, complete in it, furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "strives".

"Initiates energy": therein, what is energy? The mental initiation of energy… right effort — this is called "energy". He initiates this energy, undertakes it, practises it, develops it, cultivates it. Therefore it is said, "initiates energy".

"Exerts his mind": therein, what is the mind? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the mind". He exerts this mind, fully exerts it, supports it, upholds it. Therefore it is said, "exerts his mind".

"Endeavours": therein, what is endeavour? The mental initiation of energy… right effort — this is called "endeavour". He is endowed with this endeavour… furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "endeavours".

The Basis of Success Through Desire

And how does a monk develop the basis of success endowed with concentration through desire and the formations of endeavour? If a monk, making desire the dominant factor, obtains concentration, obtains one-pointedness of mind — this is called "concentration through desire". He generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the abandoning of evil, unwholesome things that have arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the arising of wholesome things that have not yet arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the persistence of wholesome things that have arisen, for their non-confusion, their increase, their expansion, their development, their perfection. These are called "the formations of endeavour". So there is this concentration through desire and there are these formations of endeavour. Gathering them together and summing them up, they are reckoned simply as "concentration through desire and the formations of endeavour".

Therein, what is desire? The desire, wishing, wish to act, wholesome desire for the Dhamma — this is called "desire".
Therein, what is concentration? The steadiness of the mind, its stability, its firm standing, its non-wavering, non-distraction, the state of an undistracted mind, calm, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, right concentration — this is called "concentration".
Therein, what is the formation of endeavour? The mental initiation of energy, exertion, striving forward, effort, striving, zeal, vigour, firmness, steadiness, unrelaxed striving, undiminished desire, undiminished responsibility, taking up the burden, energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy, right effort — this is called "the formation of endeavour". So he is endowed with this desire, this concentration, and this formation of endeavour, fully endowed, having reached them, fully reached them, possessed of them, complete in them, furnished with them. Therefore it is said, "endowed with concentration through desire and the formations of endeavour".

"Success": the success of those things, their prospering, succeeding, fully succeeding, gain, obtaining, attainment, full attainment, touching, realisation, achievement.
"Basis of success": for one who is such, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the aggregate of consciousness.
"Develops the basis of success": he practises those things, develops them, cultivates them. Therefore it is said, "develops the basis of success".

The Section of Questions and Answers

There are four bases of success. Here a monk develops the basis of success endowed with concentration through desire and the formations of endeavour; concentration through energy… concentration through mind… he develops the basis of success endowed with concentration through investigation and the formations of endeavour.
Of the four bases of success, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral… how many involve conflict, how many are free from conflict?
The Triads

They are wholesome only. They may be associated with pleasant feeling; they may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They are things subject to result. They are not taken up at birth and not able to be clung to. They are undefiled and not connected with defilement. They may be with thought and with examination; they may be without thought but with examination only; they may be without thought and without examination. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be accompanied by happiness; they may be accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Their causes are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. They are leading to dismantling. They belong to one in training. They are measureless. They have measureless objects. They are refined. They are fixed in rightness. They do not have the path as their object; they have the path as their cause; they do not have the path as their dominant factor. They may be arisen; they may be not arisen; they are not describable as due to arise. They may be past; they may be future; they may be present. They are not describable as having a past object, a future object, or a present object. They may be internal; they may be external; they may be both internal and external. They have external objects. They are invisible and offer no resistance.
The Pairs

The basis of success through investigation is a root; three bases of success are not roots. They have roots. They are associated with roots. The basis of success through investigation is both a root and has roots; three bases of success are not describable as being both roots and having roots; they have roots but are not roots. The basis of success through investigation is both a root and associated with roots; three bases of success are not describable as being both roots and associated with roots; they are associated with roots but are not roots. Three bases of success are not roots yet have roots; the basis of success through investigation is not describable either as being a non-root that has roots or as being a non-root without roots. They have conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. They offer no resistance. They are immaterial. They are beyond the world. They can be known by one means; they cannot be known by another. They are not mental taints. They are without mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints. They are not describable either as being mental taints and subject to mental taints, or as being subject to mental taints but not mental taints. They are not describable either as being mental taints and associated with mental taints, or as being associated with mental taints but not mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints. They are without mental taints.
They are not fetters… they are not ties… they are not floods… they are not yokes… they are not hindrances… they are not wrong grasping… they have objects. Three bases of success are not minds; the basis of success through mind is a mind. Three bases of success are mental factors; the basis of success through mind is not a mental factor. Three bases of success are associated with mind; the basis of success through mind is not describable either as associated with mind or as dissociated from mind. Three bases of success are conjoined with mind; the basis of success through mind is not describable either as conjoined with mind or as disjoined from mind. Three bases of success are originated by mind; the basis of success through mind is not originated by mind. Three bases of success arise together with mind; the basis of success through mind does not arise together with mind. Three bases of success follow along with mind; the basis of success through mind does not follow along with mind. Three bases of success are conjoined with and originated by mind; the basis of success through mind is not conjoined with and originated by mind. Three bases of success are conjoined with, originated by, and arise together with mind; the basis of success through mind is not conjoined with, originated by, and arising together with mind. Three bases of success are conjoined with, originated by, and follow along with mind; the basis of success through mind is not conjoined with, originated by, and following along with mind.
Three bases of success are external; the basis of success through mind is internal. They are not derived. They are not taken up at birth. They are not clinging… they are not defilements… they are not to be abandoned by seeing. They are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Their causes are not to be abandoned by seeing. Their causes are not to be abandoned by meditative development. They may be with thought; they may be without thought. They may be with examination; they may be without examination. They may be with joy; they may be without joy. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be not accompanied by joy. They may be accompanied by happiness; they may be not accompanied by happiness. They may be accompanied by equanimity; they may be not accompanied by equanimity. They do not belong to the sense sphere. They do not belong to the fine-material sphere. They do not belong to the immaterial sphere. They are not included in any sphere. They are leading out. They are fixed. They are unsurpassed. They are free from conflict.
The Section of Questions and Answers.
The Analysis of the Bases of Success is finished.
Analysis of the Awakening Factors
Classification According to the Discourses

There are seven awakening factors: the awakening factor of mindfulness, the awakening factor of investigation of things, the awakening factor of energy, the awakening factor of joy, the awakening factor of tranquillity, the awakening factor of concentration, the awakening factor of equanimity.

Therein, what is the awakening factor of mindfulness? Here a monk is mindful, endowed with the highest mindfulness and care; he remembers and recalls what was done long ago and said long ago — this is called "the awakening factor of mindfulness".
Dwelling thus mindful, he investigates that teaching with wisdom, examines it, and enters into a full inquiry of it — this is called "the awakening factor of investigation of things".
As he investigates that teaching with wisdom, examines it, and enters into a full inquiry of it, energy is initiated in him without slackening — this is called "the awakening factor of energy".
In one whose energy is initiated, unworldly joy arises — this is called "the awakening factor of joy".
In one whose mind is joyful, the body becomes tranquil and the mind becomes tranquil — this is called "the awakening factor of tranquillity".
In one whose body is tranquil and who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated — this is called "the awakening factor of concentration".
He is one who watches well over the mind thus concentrated, with equanimity — this is called "the awakening factor of equanimity".

There are seven awakening factors: the awakening factor of mindfulness, the awakening factor of investigation of things, the awakening factor of energy, the awakening factor of joy, the awakening factor of tranquillity, the awakening factor of concentration, the awakening factor of equanimity.

Therein, what is the awakening factor of mindfulness? There is mindfulness with regard to internal things; there is mindfulness with regard to external things. The mindfulness with regard to internal things is itself the awakening factor of mindfulness, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. The mindfulness with regard to external things is itself the awakening factor of mindfulness, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna.
Therein, what is the awakening factor of investigation of things? There is investigation of internal things; there is investigation of external things. The investigation of internal things is itself the awakening factor of investigation of things, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. The investigation of external things is itself the awakening factor of investigation of things, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna.
Therein, what is the awakening factor of energy? There is bodily energy; there is mental energy. The bodily energy is itself the awakening factor of energy, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. The mental energy is itself the awakening factor of energy, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna.
Therein, what is the awakening factor of joy? There is joy with thought and with examination; there is joy without thought and without examination. The joy with thought and with examination is itself the awakening factor of joy, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. The joy without thought and without examination is itself the awakening factor of joy, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna.
Therein, what is the awakening factor of tranquillity? There is tranquillity of the body; there is tranquillity of the mind. The tranquillity of the body is itself the awakening factor of tranquillity, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. The tranquillity of the mind is itself the awakening factor of tranquillity, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna.
Therein, what is the awakening factor of concentration? There is concentration with thought and with examination; there is concentration without thought and without examination. The concentration with thought and with examination is itself the awakening factor of concentration, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. The concentration without thought and without examination is itself the awakening factor of concentration, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna.
Therein, what is the awakening factor of equanimity? There is equanimity with regard to internal things; there is equanimity with regard to external things. The equanimity with regard to internal things is itself the awakening factor of equanimity, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna. The equanimity with regard to external things is itself the awakening factor of equanimity, and it leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna.

There are seven awakening factors: the awakening factor of mindfulness, the awakening factor of investigation of things, the awakening factor of energy, the awakening factor of joy, the awakening factor of tranquillity, the awakening factor of concentration, the awakening factor of equanimity.

Therein, what is the awakening factor of mindfulness? Here a monk develops the awakening factor of mindfulness, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, ripening in release; he develops the awakening factor of investigation of things… he develops the awakening factor of energy… he develops the awakening factor of joy… he develops the awakening factor of tranquillity… he develops the awakening factor of concentration… he develops the awakening factor of equanimity, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, ripening in release.
The Classification According to the Discourses is finished.

Therein, what is the awakening factor of joy? The joy, gladness, rejoicing, delight, mirth, merriment, felicity, elation, satisfaction of the mind, the awakening factor of joy — this is called "the awakening factor of joy".

Therein, what is the awakening factor of concentration? The steadiness of the mind… right concentration, the awakening factor of concentration, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "the awakening factor of concentration".
Therein, what is the awakening factor of equanimity? The equanimity, being equanimous, watching over with equanimity, neutrality of the mind, the awakening factor of equanimity — this is called "the awakening factor of equanimity". These are called the seven awakening factors. The remaining things are associated with the seven awakening factors.

Analysis of the Path Factors
Classification According to the Discourses
The noble eightfold path, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.

Therein, what is right view? Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the cessation of suffering, knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of suffering — this is called "right view".
Therein, what is right intention? The intention of renunciation, the intention of non-ill-will, the intention of harmlessness — this is called "right intention".
Therein, what is right speech? Abstaining from false speech, abstaining from divisive speech, abstaining from harsh speech, abstaining from idle chatter — this is called "right speech".
Therein, what is right action? Abstaining from killing living beings, abstaining from taking what is not given, abstaining from sexual misconduct — this is called "right action".
Therein, what is right livelihood? Here a noble disciple, having abandoned wrong livelihood, makes his living by right livelihood — this is called "right livelihood".
Therein, what is right effort? Here a monk generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome things that have not yet arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the abandoning of evil, unwholesome things that have arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the arising of wholesome things that have not yet arisen; he generates desire, strives, initiates energy, exerts his mind, and endeavours for the persistence of wholesome things that have arisen, for their non-confusion, their increase, their expansion, their development, their perfection — this is called "right effort".
Therein, what is right mindfulness? Here a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world; he dwells contemplating feelings in feelings — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world; he dwells contemplating the mind in the mind — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world; he dwells contemplating mental objects in mental objects — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world — this is called "right mindfulness".
Therein, what is right concentration? Here a monk, secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome things, enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, which is with thought and with examination, with joy and happiness born of seclusion; with the stilling of thought and examination, he enters and dwells in the second meditative absorption, which has inner confidence and unification of mind, is without thought and without examination, with joy and happiness born of concentration; with the fading away of joy he dwells equanimous, mindful and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body — that of which the noble ones declare, "equanimous, mindful, one who dwells happily" — he enters and dwells in the third meditative absorption; with the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of pain, and with the earlier disappearance of joy and grief, he enters and dwells in the fourth meditative absorption, which is neither painful nor pleasant and has purity of mindfulness through equanimity — this is called "right concentration".
The noble eightfold path, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.

Therein, what is right view? Here a monk develops right view, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, ripening in release; he develops right intention… he develops right speech… he develops right action… he develops right livelihood… he develops right effort… he develops right mindfulness… he develops right concentration, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, ripening in release.
The Classification According to the Discourses is finished.

Therein, what is the eightfold path? Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the meditative absorption that is beyond the world, leading out, leading to dismantling, for the abandoning of views, for reaching the first stage — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge — on that occasion there is the eightfold path: right view… right concentration.

Therein, what is right view? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view, the awakening factor of investigation of things, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right view".
Therein, what is right intention? The thinking, thought, intention, absorption, full absorption, application of the mind, right intention, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right intention".
Therein, what is right speech? The refraining from the four kinds of verbal misconduct, abstaining, desisting, abstinence, not doing, not committing, not transgressing, not overstepping the limit, destroying the bridge to them — right speech, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right speech".
Therein, what is right action? The refraining from the three kinds of bodily misconduct, abstaining, desisting, abstinence, not doing, not committing, not transgressing, not overstepping the limit, destroying the bridge to them — right action, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right action".
Therein, what is right livelihood? The refraining from wrong livelihood, abstaining, desisting, abstinence, not doing, not committing, not transgressing, not overstepping the limit, destroying the bridge to it — right livelihood, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right livelihood".
Therein, what is right effort? The mental initiation of energy… right effort, the awakening factor of energy, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right effort".
Therein, what is right mindfulness? The mindfulness, recollection… right mindfulness, the awakening factor of mindfulness, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right mindfulness".
Therein, what is right concentration? The steadiness of the mind… right concentration, the awakening factor of concentration, a path factor, included in the path — this is called "right concentration". This is called "the eightfold path". The remaining things are associated with the eightfold path.
