Analysis of Meditative Absorption
Classification According to the Discourses

Here a monk dwells restrained by the restraint of the monastic code, endowed with proper conduct and proper resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults; he trains himself, having undertaken the rules of training; he guards the doors of the faculties, knows moderation in food, and is devoted to wakefulness in the first and last parts of the night, devoted with perseverance and care to the development of the things that side with awakening. He acts with clear comprehension when going forward and returning; he acts with clear comprehension when looking ahead and looking away; he acts with clear comprehension when bending and stretching; he acts with clear comprehension when carrying the outer robe, the bowl, and the robes; he acts with clear comprehension when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; he acts with clear comprehension when defecating and urinating; he acts with clear comprehension when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and keeping silent. He resorts to a secluded dwelling place — a forest, the foot of a tree, a mountain, a glen, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a remote forest, the open air, a heap of straw — with little sound, little noise, without the breath of crowds, hidden from people, suitable for retreat. Gone to the forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut, he sits down, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body straight, and established mindfulness in front of him. Having abandoned covetousness with regard to the world, he dwells with a mind free of covetousness; he purifies his mind of covetousness. Having abandoned ill will and hatred, he dwells with a mind free of ill will, compassionate for the welfare of all living beings; he purifies his mind of ill will and hatred. Having abandoned dullness and drowsiness, he dwells free of dullness and drowsiness, percipient of light, mindful and clearly comprehending; he purifies his mind of dullness and drowsiness. Having abandoned restlessness and remorse, he dwells unagitated, with a mind inwardly stilled; he purifies his mind of restlessness and remorse. Having abandoned doubt, he dwells having crossed over doubt, without perplexity about wholesome things; he purifies his mind of doubt. Having abandoned these five hindrances, corruptions of the mind that weaken wisdom — secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome things, he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, which is with thought and with examination, with joy and happiness born of seclusion; with the stilling of thought and examination, he enters and dwells in the second meditative absorption, which has inner confidence and unification of mind, is without thought and without examination, with joy and happiness born of concentration; with the fading away of joy he dwells equanimous, mindful and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body — that of which the noble ones declare, "equanimous, mindful, one who dwells happily" — he enters and dwells in the third meditative absorption; with the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of pain, and with the earlier disappearance of joy and grief, he enters and dwells in the fourth meditative absorption, which is neither painful nor pleasant and has purity of mindfulness through equanimity; completely passing beyond perceptions of material form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, not attending to perceptions of diversity, aware that "space is infinite", he enters and dwells in the field of infinite space; completely passing beyond the field of infinite space, aware that "consciousness is infinite", he enters and dwells in the field of infinite consciousness; completely passing beyond the field of infinite consciousness, aware that "there is nothing", he enters and dwells in the field of nothingness; completely passing beyond the field of nothingness, he enters and dwells in the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
The Matrix

"Here": in this view, in this acceptance, in this preference, in this taking-up, in this teaching, in this discipline, in this teaching-and-discipline, in this doctrine, in this holy life, in this teacher's dispensation. Therefore it is said, "here".

"Monk": a monk by designation, a monk by acknowledgement, a monk because he begs, a monk because he is a beggar, a monk because he has taken up the life of begging, a monk because he wears the patched cloth, a monk because he breaks up evil, unwholesome things, a monk because he has broken up evil, unwholesome things, a monk through the partial abandoning of defilements, a monk through the complete abandoning of defilements, a monk in training, a monk beyond training, a monk neither in training nor beyond training, a foremost monk, an excellent monk, a monk in the prime, a monk of substance, a monk fully ordained by a united Order through an act with a motion and three announcements, unshakeable, fit to stand.

"The monastic code": virtue, the foundation, the beginning, conduct, self-control, restraint, release, the foremost thing for the attainment of wholesome things. "Restraint": non-transgression in body, non-transgression in speech, non-transgression in body and speech. "Restrained": he is endowed with this restraint of the monastic code, fully endowed, having reached it, fully reached it, possessed of it, complete in it, furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "restrained by the restraint of the monastic code".
"Dwells": he moves, goes on, keeps going, maintains himself, carries on, conducts himself, dwells. Therefore it is said, "dwells".

"Endowed with proper conduct and proper resort": there is proper conduct, there is improper conduct.
Therein, what is improper conduct? Transgression in body, transgression in speech, transgression in body and speech — this is called "improper conduct". All bad conduct is improper conduct. Here someone makes his living by giving bamboo, or giving leaves, or giving flowers, or giving fruits, or giving bathing supplies, or giving tooth-sticks, or by flattery, or by half-truthful talk, or by fondling children, or by carrying messages on foot, or by some other wrong means of livelihood condemned by the Buddhas — this is called "improper conduct".
Therein, what is proper conduct? Non-transgression in body, non-transgression in speech, non-transgression in body and speech — this is called "proper conduct". All restraint through virtue is proper conduct. Here someone does not make his living by giving bamboo, nor by giving leaves, nor by giving flowers, nor by giving fruits, nor by giving bathing supplies, nor by giving tooth-sticks, nor by flattery, nor by half-truthful talk, nor by fondling children, nor by carrying messages on foot, nor by any other wrong means of livelihood condemned by the Buddhas — this is called "proper conduct".

"Resort": there is proper resort, there is improper resort.
Therein, what is improper resort? Here someone frequents prostitutes, or frequents widows, or frequents grown-up unmarried women, or frequents eunuchs, or frequents nuns, or frequents taverns; he dwells associating with kings, king's ministers, teachers of other sects, and disciples of other sects, in unsuitable association; or he resorts to, frequents, and attends upon families that are without confidence and without trust, that are not like a well, that abuse and revile, that wish harm, wish ill, wish discomfort, and wish no security from bondage for monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen — this is called "improper resort".
Therein, what is proper resort? Here someone does not frequent prostitutes, does not frequent widows, does not frequent grown-up unmarried women, does not frequent eunuchs, does not frequent nuns, does not frequent taverns; he dwells not associating with kings, king's ministers, teachers of other sects, and disciples of other sects, in unsuitable association; and he resorts to, frequents, and attends upon families that have confidence and trust, that are like a well, that shine with the ochre robe, that are fanned by the breeze of sages, that wish good, wish welfare, wish comfort, and wish security from bondage for monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen — this is called "proper resort". So he is endowed with this proper conduct and this proper resort… furnished with them. Therefore it is said, "endowed with proper conduct and proper resort".

"Seeing danger in the slightest faults": therein, what are the slightest faults? Those faults that are slight, minor, light, considered light, to be dealt with by self-control, to be dealt with by restraint, to be dealt with by the arising of a right state of mind, bound up with attentiveness — these are called "the slightest faults". So in these slightest faults he is one who sees the fault, sees the danger, sees the drawback, and sees the escape. Therefore it is said, "seeing danger in the slightest faults".

"He trains himself, having undertaken the rules of training": therein, what is training? There are four trainings — for monks, the monks' training; for nuns, the nuns' training; for laymen, the laymen's training; for laywomen, the laywomen's training. These are called "the trainings". Having undertaken these trainings completely, in every respect, in every way, fully, without remainder, he proceeds in them. Therefore it is said, "he trains himself, having undertaken the rules of training".

"He guards the doors of the faculties": there is guarding the doors of the faculties, and there is not guarding the doors.
Therein, what is not guarding the doors of the faculties? Here someone, having seen a sight with the eye, grasps at its signs and grasps at its details. Since, if he dwelt with the eye faculty unrestrained, covetousness and grief, evil, unwholesome things, might flow in upon him, he does not practise for its restraint, he does not guard the eye faculty, he does not undertake restraint of the eye faculty. Having heard a sound with the ear… having smelled a smell with the nose… having tasted a taste with the tongue… having touched a tangible thing with the body… having known a mental object with the mind, he grasps at its signs and grasps at its details. Since, if he dwelt with the mind faculty unrestrained, covetousness and grief, evil, unwholesome things, might flow in upon him, he does not practise for its restraint, he does not guard the mind faculty, he does not undertake restraint of the mind faculty. The lack of guarding, lack of protection, lack of watching over, lack of restraint of these six faculties — this is called "not guarding the doors of the faculties".
Therein, what is guarding the doors of the faculties? Here someone, having seen a sight with the eye, does not grasp at its signs and does not grasp at its details. Since, if he dwelt with the eye faculty unrestrained, covetousness and grief, evil, unwholesome things, might flow in upon him, he practises for its restraint, he guards the eye faculty, he undertakes restraint of the eye faculty. Having heard a sound with the ear… having smelled a smell with the nose… having tasted a taste with the tongue… having touched a tangible thing with the body… having known a mental object with the mind, he does not grasp at its signs and does not grasp at its details. Since, if he dwelt with the mind faculty unrestrained, covetousness and grief, evil, unwholesome things, might flow in upon him, he practises for its restraint, he guards the mind faculty, he undertakes restraint of the mind faculty. The guarding, protection, watching over, and restraint of these six faculties — this is called "guarding the doors of the faculties". He is endowed with this guarding of the doors of the faculties, fully endowed… furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "he guards the doors of the faculties".

"Knows moderation in food": there is knowing moderation in food, and there is not knowing moderation in food.
Therein, what is not knowing moderation in food? Here someone takes food without reflection and unwisely — for amusement, for intoxication, for adornment, for beautification. The lack of contentment there, the lack of moderation, the lack of reflection with regard to food — this is called "not knowing moderation in food".
Therein, what is knowing moderation in food? Here someone takes food with reflection and wisely — "not for amusement, not for intoxication, not for adornment, not for beautification, but only for the persistence and maintenance of this body, for ending discomfort, for supporting the holy life, thinking: thus I shall put an end to the old feeling and not give rise to a new feeling, and I shall keep going, be blameless, and dwell in comfort." The contentment there, the moderation, the reflection with regard to food — this is called "knowing moderation in food". He is endowed with this knowing of moderation in food… furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "knows moderation in food".

And how is a monk devoted to wakefulness in the first and last parts of the night? Here a monk during the day purifies his mind of obstructive things by walking and sitting; in the first watch of the night he purifies his mind of obstructive things by walking and sitting; in the middle watch of the night he lies down on his right side in the lion's posture, placing one foot on the other, mindful and clearly comprehending, having attended to the idea of rising; in the last watch of the night, having risen, he purifies his mind of obstructive things by walking and sitting. Thus a monk is devoted to wakefulness in the first and last parts of the night.
"Perseverance": the mental initiation of energy… right effort.
"Care": the wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view.

"Devoted to the development of the things that side with awakening": therein, what are the things that side with awakening? The seven awakening factors — the awakening factor of mindfulness, the awakening factor of investigation of things, the awakening factor of energy, the awakening factor of joy, the awakening factor of tranquillity, the awakening factor of concentration, the awakening factor of equanimity. These are called "the things that side with awakening". So he practises those things that side with awakening, develops them, cultivates them. Therefore it is said, "devoted to the development of the things that side with awakening".

And how does a monk act with clear comprehension when going forward and returning, act with clear comprehension when looking ahead and looking away, act with clear comprehension when bending and stretching, act with clear comprehension when carrying the outer robe, the bowl, and the robes, act with clear comprehension when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting, act with clear comprehension when defecating and urinating, act with clear comprehension when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and keeping silent? Here a monk goes forward mindful and clearly comprehending, returns mindful and clearly comprehending, looks ahead mindful and clearly comprehending, looks away mindful and clearly comprehending, bends mindful and clearly comprehending, stretches mindful and clearly comprehending; he acts mindful and clearly comprehending; he acts mindful and clearly comprehending when carrying the outer robe, the bowl, and the robes; he acts mindful and clearly comprehending when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; he acts mindful and clearly comprehending when defecating and urinating; he acts mindful and clearly comprehending when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and keeping silent.

Therein, what is mindfulness? The mindfulness, recollection, remembering, mindfulness, bearing in mind, keeping in mind, not floating away, not forgetting; mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness — this is called "mindfulness".

"Clearly comprehending": therein, what is clear comprehension? The wisdom, understanding, investigation, close investigation, investigation of things, discerning, discrimination, differentiation, erudition, proficiency, subtlety, clarification, consideration, close examination, breadth, cleverness, guidance, insight, clear comprehension, the goad; wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom, the tower of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom; non-delusion, investigation of things, right view — this is called "clear comprehension". So he is endowed with this mindfulness and this clear comprehension… furnished with them. Thus a monk goes forward mindful and clearly comprehending, returns mindful and clearly comprehending, looks ahead mindful and clearly comprehending, looks away mindful and clearly comprehending, bends mindful and clearly comprehending, stretches mindful and clearly comprehending; he acts mindful and clearly comprehending; he acts mindful and clearly comprehending when carrying the outer robe, the bowl, and the robes; he acts mindful and clearly comprehending when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; he acts mindful and clearly comprehending when defecating and urinating; he acts with clear comprehension when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and keeping silent.

"Secluded": even if a dwelling place is nearby, if it is not crowded with householders and renunciants, then it is secluded. Even if a dwelling place is far away, if it is not crowded with householders and renunciants, then it is secluded.

"Dwelling place": a bed is a dwelling place, a chair is a dwelling place, a mattress is a dwelling place, a pillow is a dwelling place, a monastery is a dwelling place, a lean-to is a dwelling place, a mansion is a dwelling place, a watchtower is a dwelling place, a pavilion is a dwelling place, a cave-dwelling is a dwelling place, a cave is a dwelling place, the foot of a tree is a dwelling place, a bamboo thicket is a dwelling place. Or wherever monks retire — all that is a dwelling place.

"Resorts to a secluded dwelling place": he resorts to this secluded dwelling place, resorts to it fully, frequents it, frequents it closely, frequents it thoroughly. Therefore it is said, "resorts to a secluded dwelling place".
"Forest": having gone out beyond the boundary post, all that is forest.

"The foot of a tree": the foot of a tree is just the foot of a tree. A mountain is just a mountain. A glen is just a glen. A mountain cave is just a mountain cave. A charnel ground is just a charnel ground. The open air is just the open air. A heap of straw is just a heap of straw.

"Remote forest": this is a designation for distant dwelling places. "Remote forest": this is a designation for dwelling places in forest thickets. "Remote forest": this is a designation for frightening dwelling places. "Remote forest": this is a designation for hair-raising dwelling places. "Remote forest": this is a designation for outlying dwelling places. "Remote forest": this is a designation for dwelling places not near human traffic. "Remote forest": this is a designation for dwelling places hard to endure.

"With little sound": even if a dwelling place is nearby, if it is not crowded with householders and renunciants, then it has little sound. Even if a dwelling place is far away, if it is not crowded with householders and renunciants, then it has little sound.

"Little noise": what has little sound has little noise. What has little noise is without the breath of crowds. What is without the breath of crowds is hidden from people. What is hidden from people is suitable for retreat.
"Gone to the forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut": he has gone to the forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut.
"He sits down, having folded his legs crosswise": he is seated, having folded his legs crosswise.
"Having set his body straight": his body is straight, placed and directed upright.

"Having established mindfulness in front of him": therein, what is mindfulness? The mindfulness, recollection, remembering… right mindfulness — this is called "mindfulness". This mindfulness is established, well established, at the tip of the nose or at the sign of the mouth. Therefore it is said, "having established mindfulness in front of him".

"Having abandoned covetousness with regard to the world": therein, what is covetousness? The lust, passion… passion of the mind — this is called "covetousness".
Therein, what is the world? The five aggregates that can be clung to are the world — this is called "the world". This covetousness is stilled in this world, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "having abandoned covetousness with regard to the world".

"With a mind free of covetousness": therein, what is the mind? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the mind". This mind is free of covetousness. Therefore it is said, "with a mind free of covetousness".
"Dwells": he moves, goes on, keeps going, maintains himself, carries on, conducts himself, dwells. Therefore it is said, "dwells".

"He purifies his mind of covetousness": therein, what is covetousness? The lust, passion… passion of the mind — this is called "covetousness".
Therein, what is the mind? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the mind". He cleanses this mind of this covetousness, purifies it, thoroughly purifies it, frees it, releases it, fully releases it. Therefore it is said, "he purifies his mind of covetousness".

"Having abandoned ill will and hatred": there is ill will, there is hatred.
Therein, what is ill will? The resentment of the mind, repugnance, resistance, opposition, anger, being angered, great anger; hate, hating, great hating; the mind's malice, mental hatred; wrath, being wrathful, wrathfulness; hate, hating, state of hating; malice, being malicious, state of being malicious; opposition, hostility, fierceness, rudeness, the mind's dissatisfaction — this is called "ill will".
Therein, what is hatred? What is ill will is hatred; what is hatred is ill will. So this ill will and this hatred are stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "having abandoned ill will and hatred".

"With a mind free of ill will": therein, what is the mind? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the mind". This mind is free of ill will. Therefore it is said, "with a mind free of ill will".
"Dwells"… therefore it is said, "dwells".

"He purifies his mind of ill will and hatred": there is ill will, there is hatred.
Therein, what is ill will? The resentment of the mind… fierceness, rudeness, the mind's dissatisfaction — this is called "ill will".
Therein, what is hatred? What is ill will is hatred; what is hatred is ill will.
Therein, what is the mind? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the mind". He cleanses this mind of this ill will and hatred, purifies it, thoroughly purifies it, frees it, releases it, fully releases it. Therefore it is said, "he purifies his mind of ill will and hatred".

"Having abandoned dullness and drowsiness": there is dullness, there is drowsiness.
Therein, what is dullness? The mind's lack of readiness, its unworkableness, its sagging, its slumping; sloth, being slothful, the mind's slothfulness; dullness, being dull, the mind's state of dullness — this is called "dullness".
Therein, what is drowsiness? The body's lack of readiness, its unworkableness, its being covered, being enveloped, being blocked up inside; drowsiness, sleep, nodding; sleep, sleeping, state of sleeping — this is called "drowsiness". So this dullness and this drowsiness are stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "having abandoned dullness and drowsiness".

"Free of dullness and drowsiness": because that dullness and drowsiness have been given up, vomited out, let go, abandoned, relinquished, abandoned and relinquished. Therefore it is said, "free of dullness and drowsiness".
"Dwells"… therefore it is said, "dwells".

"Percipient of light": therein, what is perception? The perception, perceiving, state of having perceived — this is called "perception". This perception is luminous, open, purified, cleansed. Therefore it is said, "percipient of light".

"Mindful and clearly comprehending": therein, what is mindfulness? The mindfulness, recollection… right mindfulness — this is called "mindfulness".
Therein, what is clear comprehension? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view — this is called "clear comprehension". So he is endowed with this mindfulness and this clear comprehension… furnished with them. Therefore it is said, "mindful and clearly comprehending".

"He purifies his mind of dullness and drowsiness": there is dullness, there is drowsiness.
Therein, what is dullness… this is called "dullness".
Therein, what is drowsiness… this is called "drowsiness".
Therein, what is the mind… this is called "the mind". He cleanses this mind of this dullness and drowsiness, purifies it, thoroughly purifies it, frees it, releases it, fully releases it. Therefore it is said, "he purifies his mind of dullness and drowsiness".

"Having abandoned restlessness and remorse": there is restlessness, there is remorse.
Therein, what is restlessness? The restlessness of the mind, lack of calm, mental distraction, agitation of the mind — this is called "restlessness".
Therein, what is remorse? Perceiving what is allowable as unallowable, perceiving what is unallowable as allowable, perceiving what is blameless as blameworthy, perceiving what is blameworthy as blameless; whatever remorse of this kind there is, being remorseful, the state of remorse, the mind's regret, mental confusion — this is called "remorse". So this restlessness and this remorse are stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "having abandoned restlessness and remorse".
"Unagitated": because that restlessness and remorse have been given up, vomited out, let go, abandoned, relinquished, abandoned and relinquished. Therefore it is said, "unagitated".
"Dwells"… therefore it is said, "dwells".

"With a mind stilled": therein, what is the mind? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the mind". This mind is inwardly still, calm, quieted. Therefore it is said, "with a mind inwardly stilled".

"He purifies his mind of restlessness and remorse": there is restlessness, there is remorse.
Therein, what is restlessness? The restlessness of the mind, lack of calm, mental distraction, agitation of the mind — this is called "restlessness".
Therein, what is remorse… this is called "remorse".
Therein, what is the mind… this is called "the mind". He cleanses this mind of this restlessness and remorse, purifies it, thoroughly purifies it, frees it, releases it, fully releases it. Therefore it is said, "he purifies his mind of restlessness and remorse".

"Having abandoned doubt": therein, what is doubt? The doubt, doubting, state of doubting, perplexity, uncertainty, being of two minds, being at a crossroads, wavering, grasping at many sides, hesitation, vacillation, failure to plunge in, rigidity of the mind, mental confusion — this is called "doubt". This doubt is stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "having abandoned doubt".
"Having crossed over doubt": he has crossed this doubt, crossed over it, crossed beyond it, gone to the far shore, reached the far shore. Therefore it is said, "having crossed over doubt".

"Without perplexity about wholesome things": through this doubt he does not doubt about wholesome things, is not perplexed; he is without perplexity, free of perplexity, rid of perplexity. Therefore it is said, "without perplexity about wholesome things".

"He purifies his mind of doubt": therein, what is doubt? The doubt, doubting, state of doubting… rigidity of the mind, mental confusion — this is called "doubt".
Therein, what is the mind? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the mind". He cleanses this mind of this doubt, purifies it, thoroughly purifies it, frees it, releases it, fully releases it. Therefore it is said, "he purifies his mind of doubt".

"Having abandoned these five hindrances": these five hindrances are stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "having abandoned these five hindrances".
"Corruptions of the mind": these five hindrances are corruptions of the mind.
"That weaken wisdom": because of these five hindrances, wisdom not yet arisen does not arise, and wisdom that has arisen ceases. Therefore it is said, "that weaken wisdom".

"Secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome things": therein, what are sense pleasures? Desire is a sense pleasure, lust is a sense pleasure, desire-and-lust is a sense pleasure, intention is a sense pleasure, lust is a sense pleasure, intention-and-lust is a sense pleasure — these are called "sense pleasures".
Therein, what are unwholesome things? Sense desire, ill will, dullness, drowsiness, restlessness, remorse, doubt — these are called "unwholesome things". So he is secluded from these sense pleasures and these unwholesome things. Therefore it is said, "secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome things".

"With thought and with examination": there is thought, there is examination.
Therein, what is thought? The thinking, thought, intention, absorption, full absorption, application of the mind, right intention — this is called "thought".
Therein, what is examination? The moving about, examination, following up, scrutiny, the mind's continuous connection and careful consideration — this is called examination. So he is endowed with this thought and this examination… furnished with them. Therefore it is said, "with thought and with examination".

"Born of seclusion": thought, examination, joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind — these are born in this seclusion, brought forth, produced, brought into being, made manifest. Therefore it is said, "born of seclusion".

"Joy and happiness": there is joy, there is happiness.
Therein, what is joy? The joy, gladness, rejoicing, delight, mirth, merriment, felicity, elation, satisfaction of the mind — this is called "joy".
Therein, what is happiness? Mental comfort, mental happiness, the comfortable happy experience born of mind-contact, the comfortable happy feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "happiness". This happiness is accompanied by this joy, arisen together with it, conjoined with it, associated with it. Therefore it is said, "joy and happiness".
"First": first in numerical order. It is first because one attains it first.
"Meditative absorption": thought, examination, joy, happiness, one-pointedness of mind.
"Enters": the gaining of the first meditative absorption, its obtaining, attainment, full attainment, touching, realisation, achievement.
"Dwells"… therefore it is said, "dwells".

"With the stilling of thought and examination": there is thought, there is examination.
Therein, what is thought? The thinking, thought… right intention — this is called "thought".
Therein, what is examination? The moving about, examination, following up, scrutiny, the mind's continuous connection and careful consideration — this is called "examination". So this thought and this examination are stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "with the stilling of thought and examination".
"Inner": what is internal, one's own.
"Confidence": the confidence, trusting, reliance, full confidence.
"Unification of mind": the steadiness of the mind… right concentration.

"Without thought and without examination": there is thought, there is examination.
Therein, what is thought? The thinking, thought… right intention — this is called "thought".
Therein, what is examination? The moving about, following along, examination, following up, scrutiny, the mind's continuous connection and careful consideration — this is called "examination". So this thought and this examination are stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "without thought and without examination".

"Born of concentration": confidence, joy, and happiness — these are born in this concentration, brought forth, produced, brought into being, made manifest. Therefore it is said, "born of concentration".

"Joy and happiness": there is joy, there is happiness.
Therein, what is joy… this is called "joy".
Therein, what is happiness… this is called "happiness". This happiness is accompanied by this joy, arisen together with it, conjoined with it, associated with it. Therefore it is said, "joy and happiness".
"Second": second in numerical order. It is second because one attains it second.
"Meditative absorption": confidence, joy and happiness, one-pointedness of mind.
"Enters": the gaining of the second meditative absorption, its obtaining, attainment, full attainment, touching, realisation, achievement.
"Dwells"… therefore it is said, "dwells".

"With the fading away of joy": therein, what is joy? The joy, gladness, rejoicing, delight, mirth, merriment, felicity, elation, satisfaction of the mind — this is called "joy". This joy is stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "with the fading away of joy".

"Equanimous": therein, what is equanimity? The equanimity, being equanimous, watching over with equanimity, neutrality of the mind — this is called "equanimity". He is endowed with this equanimity… furnished with it. Therefore it is said, "equanimous".
"Dwells"… therefore it is said, "dwells".

"Mindful and clearly comprehending": therein, what is mindfulness? The mindfulness, recollection… right mindfulness — this is called "mindfulness".
Therein, what is clear comprehension? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view — this is called "clear comprehension". So he is endowed with this mindfulness and this clear comprehension… furnished with them. Therefore it is said, "mindful and clearly comprehending".

"And experiences happiness with the body": therein, what is happiness? Mental comfort, mental happiness, the comfortable happy experience born of mind-contact, the comfortable happy feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "happiness".
Therein, what is the body? The aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the aggregate of consciousness — this is called "the body". He experiences this happiness with this body. Therefore it is said, "and experiences happiness with the body".

"That of which the noble ones declare": therein, who are the noble ones? The Buddhas and the Buddhas' disciples are called the noble ones. They declare this, teach it, make it known, establish it, disclose it, analyse it, make it plain, proclaim it. Therefore it is said, "that of which the noble ones declare".

"Equanimous, mindful, one who dwells happily": therein, what is equanimity? The equanimity, being equanimous, watching over with equanimity, neutrality of the mind — this is called "equanimity".
Therein, what is mindfulness? The mindfulness, recollection… right mindfulness — this is called "mindfulness".
Therein, what is happiness? Mental comfort, mental happiness, the comfortable happy experience born of mind-contact, the comfortable happy feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "happiness". So, furnished with this equanimity, this mindfulness, and this happiness, he moves, goes on, keeps going, maintains himself, carries on, conducts himself, dwells. Therefore it is said, "equanimous, mindful, one who dwells happily".
"Third": third in numerical order. It is third because one attains it third.
"Meditative absorption": equanimity, mindfulness, clear comprehension, happiness, one-pointedness of mind.
"Enters": the gaining of the third meditative absorption, its obtaining, attainment, full attainment, touching, realisation, achievement.
"Dwells"… therefore it is said, "dwells".

"With the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of pain": there is happiness, there is pain.
Therein, what is happiness? Bodily comfort, bodily happiness, the comfortable happy experience born of body-contact, the comfortable happy feeling born of body-contact — this is called "happiness".
Therein, what is pain? Bodily discomfort, bodily pain, the uncomfortable painful experience born of body-contact, the uncomfortable painful feeling born of body-contact — this is called "pain". So this happiness and this pain are stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "with the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of pain".

"With the earlier disappearance of joy and grief": there is joy, there is grief.
Therein, what is joy? Mental comfort, mental happiness, the comfortable happy experience born of mind-contact, the comfortable happy feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "joy".
Therein, what is grief? Mental discomfort, mental pain, the uncomfortable painful experience born of mind-contact, the uncomfortable painful feeling born of mind-contact — this is called "grief". So this joy and this grief are already earlier stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "with the earlier disappearance of joy and grief".

"Neither painful nor pleasant": mental experience that is neither comfortable nor uncomfortable, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant experience born of mind-contact, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mind-contact. Therefore it is said, "neither painful nor pleasant".

"Purity of mindfulness through equanimity": therein, what is equanimity? The equanimity, being equanimous, watching over with equanimity, neutrality of the mind — this is called "equanimity".
Therein, what is mindfulness? The mindfulness, recollection… right mindfulness — this is called "mindfulness". This mindfulness is opened up by this equanimity, purified, cleansed. Therefore it is said, "purity of mindfulness through equanimity".
"Fourth": fourth in numerical order. It is fourth because one attains it fourth.
"Meditative absorption": equanimity, mindfulness, one-pointedness of mind.
"Enters": the gaining of the fourth meditative absorption, its obtaining, attainment, full attainment, touching, realisation, achievement.
"Dwells"… therefore it is said, "dwells".

"Completely passing beyond perceptions of material form": therein, what are perceptions of material form? The perception, perceiving, state of having perceived of one who has attained a fine-material-sphere attainment, or of one who has been reborn there, or of one dwelling happily in this very life — these are called "perceptions of material form". He has passed beyond these perceptions of material form, transcended them, gone completely beyond them. Therefore it is said, "completely passing beyond perceptions of material form".

"With the disappearance of perceptions of resistance": therein, what are perceptions of resistance? Perception of sights, perception of sounds… perception of tangible things — these are called perceptions of resistance. These perceptions of resistance are stilled, calmed, quieted, gone to rest, completely gone to rest, extinguished, fully extinguished, dried up, completely dried up, brought to an end. Therefore it is said, "with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance".

"Not attending to perceptions of diversity": therein, what are perceptions of diversity? The perception, perceiving, state of having perceived of one who has not attained, who possesses the mind element or possesses the mind-consciousness element — these are called "perceptions of diversity". He does not attend to these perceptions of diversity. Therefore it is said, "not attending to perceptions of diversity".

"Space is infinite": therein, what is space? The space, what belongs to space, the void, what belongs to the void, the gap, what belongs to the gap, untouched by the four great elements — this is called "space". He places his mind in that space, settles it there, pervades it as infinite. Therefore it is said, "space is infinite".
"The field of infinite space": the mind and mental factors of one who has attained the field of infinite space, or of one who has been reborn there, or of one dwelling happily in this very life.
"Enters": the gaining of the field of infinite space, its obtaining, attainment, full attainment, touching, realisation, achievement.
"Dwells"… therefore it is said, "dwells".

"Completely passing beyond the field of infinite space": he has passed beyond this field of infinite space, transcended it, gone completely beyond it. Therefore it is said, "completely passing beyond the field of infinite space".
"Consciousness is infinite": he attends to that same space as touched by consciousness, pervades it as infinite. Therefore it is said, "consciousness is infinite".

"The field of infinite consciousness": the mind and mental factors of one who has attained the field of infinite consciousness, or of one who has been reborn there, or of one dwelling happily in this very life.
"Enters": the gaining of the field of infinite consciousness, its obtaining, attainment, full attainment, touching, realisation, achievement.
"Dwells"… therefore it is said, "dwells".

"Completely passing beyond the field of infinite consciousness": he has passed beyond this field of infinite consciousness, transcended it, gone completely beyond it. Therefore it is said, "completely passing beyond the field of infinite consciousness".
"There is nothing": he makes that same consciousness disappear, makes it vanish, makes it disappear in between, and sees "there is nothing". Therefore it is said, "there is nothing".
"The field of nothingness": the mind and mental factors of one who has attained the field of nothingness, or of one who has been reborn there, or of one dwelling happily in this very life.
"Enters": the gaining of the field of nothingness, its obtaining, attainment, full attainment, touching, realisation, achievement.
"Dwells"… therefore it is said, "dwells".

"Completely passing beyond the field of nothingness": he has passed beyond this field of nothingness, transcended it, gone completely beyond it. Therefore it is said, "completely passing beyond the field of nothingness".
"Neither percipient nor non-percipient": he attends to that same field of nothingness as peaceful and develops the attainment with a residue of formations. Therefore it is said, "neither percipient nor non-percipient".

"The field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception": the mind and mental factors of one who has attained the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, or of one who has been reborn there, or of one dwelling happily in this very life.
"Enters": the gaining of the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, its obtaining, attainment, full attainment, touching, realisation, achievement.

"Dwells": he moves, goes on, keeps going, maintains himself, carries on, conducts himself, dwells. Therefore it is said, "dwells".
The Classification According to the Discourses is finished.

There are four meditative absorptions: the first meditative absorption, the second meditative absorption, the third meditative absorption, the fourth meditative absorption.

Therein, what is the first meditative absorption? Here a monk, on the occasion when he develops the path for rebirth in the fine-material sphere — secluded from sense pleasures… he enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption on the earth device — on that occasion there is the five-factored meditative absorption: thought, examination, joy, happiness, one-pointedness of mind. This is called "the first meditative absorption". The remaining things are associated with the meditative absorption.

The Section of Questions and Answers

There are four meditative absorptions. Here a monk, secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome things, enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, which is with thought and with examination, with joy and happiness born of seclusion… with the stilling of thought and examination, he enters and dwells in the second meditative absorption, which has inner confidence and unification of mind, is without thought and without examination, with joy and happiness born of concentration… with the fading away of joy he dwells equanimous, mindful and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body — that of which the noble ones declare, "equanimous, mindful, one who dwells happily" — he enters and dwells in the third meditative absorption… with the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of pain, and with the earlier disappearance of joy and grief, he enters and dwells in the fourth meditative absorption, which is neither painful nor pleasant and has purity of mindfulness through equanimity.
Of the four meditative absorptions, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral… how many involve conflict, how many are free from conflict?
The Triads

They may be wholesome; they may be neutral. Three meditative absorptions — setting aside the pleasant feeling arisen in them — are associated with pleasant feeling; the fourth meditative absorption — setting aside the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arisen in it — is associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They may be results; they may be things subject to result; they may be neither results nor things subject to result. They may be taken up at birth and able to be clung to; they may be not taken up at birth but able to be clung to; they may be not taken up at birth and not able to be clung to. They may be undefiled but connected with defilement; they may be undefiled and not connected with defilement. The first meditative absorption — setting aside the thought and examination arisen in it — is with thought and with examination; three meditative absorptions are without thought and without examination. Two meditative absorptions — setting aside the joy arisen in them — are accompanied by joy; three meditative absorptions — setting aside the happiness arisen in them — are accompanied by happiness; the fourth meditative absorption — setting aside the equanimity arisen in it — is accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Their causes are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. They may be leading to accumulation; they may be leading to dismantling; they may be leading neither to accumulation nor to dismantling. They may belong to one in training; they may belong to one beyond training; they may belong to one neither in training nor beyond training. They may be expanded; they may be measureless. Three meditative absorptions are not describable either as having limited objects or as having expanded objects; they may have measureless objects, or they may not be describable as having measureless objects; the fourth meditative absorption may have a limited object, may have an expanded object, may have a measureless object, or may not be describable as having a limited object, an expanded object, or a measureless object. They may be middling; they may be refined. They may be fixed in rightness; they may be unfixed. Three meditative absorptions do not have the path as their object; they may have the path as their cause; they may have the path as their dominant factor; or they may not be describable either as having the path as their cause or as having the path as their dominant factor; the fourth meditative absorption may have the path as its object, may have the path as its cause, may have the path as its dominant factor, or may not be describable as having the path as its object, as its cause, or as its dominant factor. They may be arisen; they may be not arisen; they may be due to arise. They may be past; they may be future; they may be present. Three meditative absorptions are not describable as having a past object, a future object, or a present object; the fourth meditative absorption may have a past object, may have a future object, may have a present object, or may not be describable as having a past object, a future object, or a present object. They may be internal; they may be external; they may be both internal and external. Three meditative absorptions have external objects; the fourth meditative absorption may have an internal object, may have an external object, may have both an internal and external object, or may not be describable as having an internal object, an external object, or both an internal and external object. They are invisible and offer no resistance.
The Pairs

They are not roots; they have roots; they are associated with roots; they are not describable as being "both roots and having roots"; they have roots but are not roots; they are not describable as being "both roots and associated with roots"; they are associated with roots but are not roots; they are not roots yet have roots.
They have conditions; they are conditioned; they are invisible; they offer no resistance; they are immaterial; they may be worldly; they may be beyond the world; they can be known by one means; they cannot be known by another.
They are not mental taints; they may be subject to mental taints; they may be without mental taints; they are dissociated from mental taints; they are not describable as being "both mental taints and subject to mental taints"; they may be subject to mental taints but not mental taints, or they may not be describable as being "subject to mental taints but not mental taints". They are not describable either as being "both mental taints and associated with mental taints", or as being "associated with mental taints but not mental taints". They may be dissociated from mental taints and subject to mental taints; they may be dissociated from mental taints and without mental taints.
They are not fetters… they are not ties… they are not floods… they are not yokes… they are not hindrances… they are not wrong grasping… they have objects; they are not minds; they are mental factors; they are associated with mind; they are conjoined with mind; they are originated by mind; they arise together with mind; they follow along with mind; they are conjoined with and originated by mind; they are conjoined with, originated by, and arise together with mind; they are conjoined with, originated by, and follow along with mind; they are external; they are not derived; they may be taken up at birth; they may be not taken up at birth.
They are not clinging… they are not defilements… they are not to be abandoned by seeing; they are not to be abandoned by meditative development; their causes are not to be abandoned by seeing; their causes are not to be abandoned by meditative development. The first meditative absorption — setting aside the thought arisen in it — is with thought; three meditative absorptions are without thought. The first meditative absorption — setting aside the examination arisen in it — is with examination; three meditative absorptions are without examination. Two meditative absorptions — setting aside the joy arisen in them — are with joy; two meditative absorptions are without joy. Two meditative absorptions — setting aside the joy arisen in them — are accompanied by joy; two meditative absorptions are not accompanied by joy. Three meditative absorptions — setting aside the happiness arisen in them — are accompanied by happiness; the fourth meditative absorption is not accompanied by happiness. The fourth meditative absorption — setting aside the equanimity arisen in it — is accompanied by equanimity; three meditative absorptions are not accompanied by equanimity. They do not belong to the sense sphere; they may belong to the fine-material sphere, or they may not belong to the fine-material sphere; three meditative absorptions do not belong to the immaterial sphere; the fourth meditative absorption may belong to the immaterial sphere, or it may not belong to the immaterial sphere. They may be included in a sphere; they may be not included in any sphere. They may be leading out; they may be not leading out. They may be fixed; they may be unfixed. They may be surpassable; they may be unsurpassed. They are free from conflict.
The Section of Questions and Answers.
The Analysis of Meditative Absorption is finished.
Analysis of the Measureless States
Classification According to the Discourses

There are four measureless states. Here a monk dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. So above, below, across, everywhere, regarding all as himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness — abundant, expanded, measureless, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by compassion, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. So above, below, across, everywhere, regarding all as himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by compassion — abundant, expanded, measureless, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. So above, below, across, everywhere, regarding all as himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy — abundant, expanded, measureless, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by equanimity, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. So above, below, across, everywhere, regarding all as himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity — abundant, expanded, measureless, without hostility, without ill will.
Loving-Kindness

And how does a monk dwell pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness? Just as, on seeing one person who is dear and pleasing, he would feel loving-kindness, in the same way he pervades all beings with loving-kindness.
Therein, what is loving-kindness? The friendliness towards beings, being friendly, the state of friendliness, the liberation of mind through loving-kindness — this is called "loving-kindness".
Therein, what is the mind? The mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the mind". This mind is accompanied by this loving-kindness, arisen together with it, conjoined with it, associated with it. Therefore it is said, "with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness".
"One direction": the eastern direction, or the western direction, or the northern direction, or the southern direction, or above, or below, or across, or an intermediate direction.
"Pervading": pervading and resolving upon.
"Dwells": he moves, goes on, keeps going, maintains himself, carries on, conducts himself, dwells. Therefore it is said, "dwells".
"Likewise the second": just as the first direction, so the second direction, so the third direction, so the fourth direction, so above, so below, so across, so the intermediate directions.

"Everywhere, regarding all as himself, the entire world": completely, in every respect, in every way, fully, without remainder. This is an all-inclusive expression — "everywhere, regarding all as himself, the entire world".

"With a mind accompanied by loving-kindness": therein, what is loving-kindness? The friendliness towards beings, being friendly, the state of friendliness, the liberation of mind through loving-kindness — this is called "loving-kindness".
Therein, what is the mind? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the mind". This mind is accompanied by this loving-kindness, arisen together with it, conjoined with it, associated with it. Therefore it is said, "with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness".
"Abundant": what is abundant is expanded; what is expanded is measureless; what is measureless is without hostility; what is without hostility is without ill will.
"Pervading": pervading and resolving upon.
"Dwells"… therefore it is said, "dwells".
Compassion

Therein, what is compassion? The compassion towards beings, being compassionate, the state of compassion, the liberation of mind through compassion — this is called "compassion".
Therein, what is the mind? The mind, mentality, mental activity… the corresponding mind-consciousness element — this is called "the mind". This mind is accompanied by this compassion, arisen together with it, conjoined with it, associated with it. Therefore it is said, "with a mind accompanied by compassion".

"With a mind accompanied by compassion": therein, what is compassion? The compassion towards beings, being compassionate, the state of compassion, the liberation of mind through compassion — this is called "compassion".

He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by compassion, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth; so above, below, across, everywhere, regarding all as himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by compassion — abundant, expanded, measureless, without hostility, without ill will. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by equanimity, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth; so above, below, across, everywhere, regarding all as himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity — abundant, expanded, measureless, without hostility, without ill will.
Of the four measureless states, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral… how many involve conflict, how many are free from conflict?
The Triads

They may be wholesome; they may be neutral. Three measureless states are associated with pleasant feeling; equanimity is associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They may be results; they may be things subject to result; they may be neither results nor things subject to result. They may be taken up at birth and able to be clung to; they may be not taken up at birth but able to be clung to. They are undefiled but connected with defilement. Three measureless states may be with thought and with examination, may be without thought but with examination only, or may be without thought and without examination; equanimity is without thought and without examination. Three measureless states may be accompanied by joy, may be accompanied by happiness, are not accompanied by equanimity, or may not be describable as accompanied by joy; equanimity is accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Their causes are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. They may be leading to accumulation; they may be leading neither to accumulation nor to dismantling. They belong to one neither in training nor beyond training. They are expanded. They are not describable as having limited objects, expanded objects, or measureless objects. They are middling. They are unfixed. They are not describable as having the path as their object, as having the path as their cause, or as having the path as their dominant factor. They may be arisen; they may be not arisen; they may be due to arise. They may be past; they may be future; they may be present. They are not describable as having a past object, a future object, or a present object. They may be internal; they may be external; they may be both internal and external. They have external objects. They are invisible and offer no resistance.
The Pairs

Loving-kindness is a root; three measureless states are not roots; they have roots; they are associated with roots. Loving-kindness is both a root and has roots; three measureless states are not describable as being both roots and having roots; they have roots but are not roots. Loving-kindness is both a root and associated with roots; three measureless states are not describable as being both roots and associated with roots; they are associated with roots but are not roots. Three measureless states are not roots yet have roots; loving-kindness is not describable either as being a non-root that has roots or as being a non-root without roots.
They have conditions; they are conditioned; they are invisible; they offer no resistance; they are immaterial; they are worldly; they can be known by one means; they cannot be known by another. They are not mental taints; they are subject to mental taints; they are dissociated from mental taints; they are not describable as being both mental taints and subject to mental taints; they are subject to mental taints but not mental taints; they are not describable either as being mental taints and associated with mental taints, or as being associated with mental taints but not mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints but subject to mental taints.
They are not fetters… they are not ties… they are not floods… they are not yokes… they are not hindrances… they are not wrong grasping… they have objects; they are not minds; they are mental factors; they are associated with mind; they are conjoined with mind; they are originated by mind; they arise together with mind; they follow along with mind; they are conjoined with and originated by mind; they are conjoined with, originated by, and arise together with mind; they are conjoined with, originated by, and follow along with mind; they are external; they are not derived; they may be taken up at birth; they may be not taken up at birth.
They are not clinging… they are not defilements… they are not to be abandoned by seeing; they are not to be abandoned by meditative development; their causes are not to be abandoned by seeing; their causes are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Three measureless states may be with thought or may be without thought; equanimity is without thought. Three measureless states may be with examination or may be without examination; equanimity is without examination. Three measureless states may be with joy or may be without joy; equanimity is without joy. Three measureless states may be accompanied by joy or may be not accompanied by joy; equanimity is not accompanied by joy. Three measureless states are accompanied by happiness; equanimity is not accompanied by happiness. Equanimity is accompanied by equanimity; three measureless states are not accompanied by equanimity. They do not belong to the sense sphere; they belong to the fine-material sphere; they do not belong to the immaterial sphere; they are included in a sphere; they are not leading out; they are unfixed; they are surpassable; they are free from conflict.

The Analysis of the Measureless States is finished.

The Triads

They are wholesome only. They may be associated with pleasant feeling; they may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. They are things subject to result. They are not taken up at birth but able to be clung to. They are undefiled but connected with defilement. They are with thought and with examination. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be accompanied by happiness; they may be accompanied by equanimity.
They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Their causes are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. They are leading to accumulation. They belong to one neither in training nor beyond training. They are limited. They have limited objects. They are middling. They are unfixed. They are not describable as having the path as their object, as having the path as their cause, or as having the path as their dominant factor. They may be arisen; they may be not arisen; they are not describable as due to arise. They may be past; they may be future; they may be present. They have present objects. They may be internal; they may be external; they may be both internal and external. They have external objects. They are invisible and offer no resistance.
The Pairs

They are not roots; they have roots; they are associated with roots. They are not describable as being "both roots and having roots"; they have roots but are not roots. They are not describable as being "both roots and associated with roots"; they are associated with roots but are not roots. They are not roots yet have roots. They have conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. They offer no resistance. They are immaterial. They are worldly. They can be known by one means; they cannot be known by another.
They are not mental taints; they are subject to mental taints; they are dissociated from mental taints. They are not describable as being "both mental taints and subject to mental taints"; they are subject to mental taints but not mental taints. They are not describable either as being "mental taints and associated with mental taints", or as being "associated with mental taints but not mental taints". They are dissociated from mental taints but subject to mental taints. They are not fetters… they are not ties… they are not floods… they are not yokes… they are not hindrances… they are not wrong grasping… they have objects. They are not minds. They are mental factors. They are associated with mind. They are conjoined with mind. They are originated by mind. They arise together with mind. They follow along with mind. They are conjoined with and originated by mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and arise together with mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and follow along with mind. They are external. They are not derived. They are not taken up at birth. They are not clinging… they are not defilements.
They are not to be abandoned by seeing. They are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Their causes are not to be abandoned by seeing. Their causes are not to be abandoned by meditative development. They are with thought. They are with examination. They may be with joy; they may be without joy. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be not accompanied by joy. They may be accompanied by happiness; they may be not accompanied by happiness. They may be accompanied by equanimity; they may be not accompanied by equanimity. They belong to the sense sphere. They do not belong to the fine-material sphere. They do not belong to the immaterial sphere. They are included in a sphere. They are not leading out. They are unfixed. They are surpassable. They are free from conflict.

Classification According to the Discourses
The Summary Section

There are four analytical knowledges: the analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of principles, the analytical knowledge of language, the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. Knowledge with regard to meaning is the analytical knowledge of meaning; knowledge with regard to principles is the analytical knowledge of principles; knowledge with regard to the expression of the language of those principles is the analytical knowledge of language; knowledge with regard to knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. This is the summary section.

Therein, what is the analytical knowledge of principles? Here a monk knows the teaching — the discourses, the mixed prose-and-verse, the expositions, the verses, the inspired utterances, the "thus it was said" texts, the birth stories, the marvellous accounts, the question-and-answer texts. This is called "the analytical knowledge of principles". He knows the meaning of each thing that has been spoken — "this is the meaning of this saying, this is the meaning of this saying". This is called "the analytical knowledge of meaning". Knowledge with regard to the expression of the language of those principles is the analytical knowledge of language. Knowledge with regard to knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. This is the scripture section.

Of the four analytical knowledges, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral… how many involve conflict, how many are free from conflict?
The Triads

They may be wholesome; they may be neutral. They may be associated with pleasant feeling; they may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Three analytical knowledges may be things subject to result, or may be neither results nor things subject to result; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be a result, may be a thing subject to result, or may be neither a result nor a thing subject to result. Three analytical knowledges are not taken up at birth but able to be clung to; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be not taken up at birth but able to be clung to, or may be not taken up at birth and not able to be clung to. Three analytical knowledges are undefiled but connected with defilement; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be undefiled but connected with defilement, or may be undefiled and not connected with defilement.
Three analytical knowledges are with thought and with examination; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be with thought and with examination, may be without thought but with examination only, or may be without thought and without examination. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be accompanied by happiness; they may be accompanied by equanimity. They are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Their causes are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development.
Three analytical knowledges may be leading to accumulation, or may be leading neither to accumulation nor to dismantling; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be leading to accumulation, may be leading to dismantling, or may be leading neither to accumulation nor to dismantling.
Three analytical knowledges belong to one neither in training nor beyond training; the analytical knowledge of meaning may belong to one in training, may belong to one beyond training, or may belong to one neither in training nor beyond training. Three analytical knowledges are limited; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be limited, or may be measureless. The analytical knowledge of language has a limited object; three analytical knowledges may have limited objects, may have expanded objects, or may have measureless objects.
Three analytical knowledges are middling; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be middling, or may be refined. Three analytical knowledges are unfixed; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be fixed in rightness, or may be unfixed. The analytical knowledge of language is not describable as having the path as its object, as having the path as its cause, or as having the path as its dominant factor; the analytical knowledge of meaning does not have the path as its object, may have the path as its cause, may have the path as its dominant factor, or may not be describable either as having the path as its cause or as having the path as its dominant factor; two analytical knowledges may have the path as their object, do not have the path as their cause, may have the path as their dominant factor, or may not be describable either as having the path as their object or as having the path as their dominant factor.
Three analytical knowledges may be arisen, or may be not arisen; they are not describable as due to arise; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be arisen, may be not arisen, or may be due to arise. They may be past; they may be future; they may be present. The analytical knowledge of language has a present object; two analytical knowledges may have a past object, may have a future object, or may have a present object; the analytical knowledge of meaning may have a past object, may have a future object, may have a present object, or may not be describable as having a past object, a future object, or a present object. They may be internal; they may be external; they may be both internal and external. The analytical knowledge of language has an external object; three analytical knowledges may have internal objects, may have external objects, or may have both internal and external objects. They are invisible and offer no resistance.
The Pairs

They are roots. They have roots. They are associated with roots. They are both roots and have roots. They are both roots and associated with roots. They are not describable either as being non-roots that have roots or as being non-roots without roots.
They have conditions. They are conditioned. They are invisible. They offer no resistance. They are immaterial. Three analytical knowledges are worldly; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be worldly, or may be beyond the world. They can be known by one means; they cannot be known by another.
They are not mental taints. Three analytical knowledges are subject to mental taints; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be subject to mental taints, or may be without mental taints. They are dissociated from mental taints. Three analytical knowledges are not describable as being both mental taints and subject to mental taints; they are subject to mental taints but not mental taints. The analytical knowledge of meaning is not describable as being both a mental taint and subject to mental taints; it may be subject to mental taints but not a mental taint, or it may not be describable as being subject to mental taints but not a mental taint. They are not describable either as being mental taints and associated with mental taints, or as being associated with mental taints but not mental taints. Three analytical knowledges are dissociated from mental taints but subject to mental taints; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be dissociated from mental taints and subject to mental taints, or may be dissociated from mental taints and without mental taints.
They are not fetters… they are not ties… they are not floods… they are not yokes… they are not hindrances… they are not wrong grasping… they have objects. They are not minds. They are mental factors. They are associated with mind. They are conjoined with mind. They are originated by mind. They arise together with mind. They follow along with mind. They are conjoined with and originated by mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and arise together with mind. They are conjoined with, originated by, and follow along with mind. They are external. They are not derived. They are not taken up at birth.
They are not clinging… they are not defilements… they are not to be abandoned by seeing. They are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Their causes are not to be abandoned by seeing. Their causes are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Three analytical knowledges are with thought; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be with thought, or may be without thought. Three analytical knowledges are with examination; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be with examination, or may be without examination. They may be with joy; they may be without joy. They may be accompanied by joy; they may be not accompanied by joy. They may be accompanied by happiness; they may be not accompanied by happiness. They may be accompanied by equanimity; they may be not accompanied by equanimity. Three analytical knowledges belong to the sense sphere; the analytical knowledge of meaning may belong to the sense sphere, or may not belong to the sense sphere. They do not belong to the fine-material sphere. They do not belong to the immaterial sphere. Three analytical knowledges are included in a sphere; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be included in a sphere, or may be not included in any sphere. Three analytical knowledges are not leading out; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be leading out, or may be not leading out. Three analytical knowledges are unfixed; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be fixed, or may be unfixed. Three analytical knowledges are surpassable; the analytical knowledge of meaning may be surpassable, or may be unsurpassed. They are free from conflict.

(8) The four analytical knowledges
(9) The four modes of practice
(10) The four objects
(11) Knowledge of aging and death, knowledge of the origin of aging and death, knowledge of the cessation of aging and death, knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of aging and death
(12-21) Knowledge of birth… knowledge of existence… knowledge of clinging… knowledge of craving… knowledge of feeling… knowledge of contact… knowledge of the six sense-fields… knowledge of mentality and material form… knowledge of consciousness… knowledge of formations, knowledge of the origin of formations, knowledge of the cessation of formations, knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of formations. Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of four.

The ground of knowledge by way of five:
(1) Five-factored right concentration (2) five-knowledged right concentration
Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of five.

The ground of knowledge by way of six:
(1) Wisdom in the six direct knowledges
Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of six.
The Matrix of Sevens

The ground of knowledge by way of seven:
(1) The seventy-seven grounds of knowledge
Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of seven.

The ground of knowledge by way of eight:
(1) Wisdom in the four paths and in the four fruits
Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of eight.

The ground of knowledge by way of nine:
(1) Wisdom in the nine successive dwelling attainments
