The Matrix of Tens

The ground of knowledge by way of ten: the ten Tathāgata-powers of the Tathāgata, endowed with which the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā. Which ten?
(1) Here the Tathāgata knows as it really is the possible as possible and the impossible as impossible. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the possible as possible and the impossible as impossible — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā.
(2) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the result of past, future, and present undertakings of action, according to circumstance and according to cause. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the result of past, future, and present undertakings of action, according to circumstance and according to cause — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā.
(3) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the way that leads everywhere. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the way that leads everywhere — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā.
(4) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the world with its many and different elements. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the world with its many and different elements — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā.
(5) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the different inclinations of beings. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the different inclinations of beings — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā.
(6) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the higher and lower state of the faculties of other beings, of other persons. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the higher and lower state of the faculties of other beings, of other persons — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā.
(7) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the defilement, the cleansing, and the emergence in the meditative absorptions, liberations, concentrations, and attainments. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the defilement, the cleansing, and the emergence in the meditative absorptions, liberations, concentrations, and attainments — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā.
(8) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the recollection of past lives. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the recollection of past lives — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā.
(9) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the passing away and rebirth of beings. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the passing away and rebirth of beings — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā.
(10) Further, the Tathāgata knows as it really is the destruction of the mental taints. That the Tathāgata knows as it really is the destruction of the mental taints — this too is a Tathāgata-power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā. These are the ten Tathāgata-powers of the Tathāgata, endowed with which the Tathāgata claims the place of the bull, roars his lion's roar in the assemblies, and sets rolling the wheel of Brahmā.
Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of ten.
The Matrix
The Exposition of the Ones

The five kinds of consciousness are simply not roots, simply without roots, simply dissociated from roots, simply having conditions, simply conditioned, simply immaterial, simply worldly, simply subject to mental taints, simply able to be bound by fetters, simply able to be bound by ties, simply able to be swept by floods, simply able to be bound by yokes, simply able to be obstructed by hindrances, simply able to be wrongly grasped, simply able to be clung to, simply able to be defiled, simply neutral, simply having objects, simply not mental factors, simply results, simply taken up at birth and able to be clung to, simply undefiled but connected with defilement, simply not with thought and with examination, simply not without thought but with examination only, simply without thought and without examination, simply not accompanied by joy, simply to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development, simply having causes to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development, simply leading neither to accumulation nor to dismantling, simply belonging to one neither in training nor beyond training, simply limited, simply of the sense sphere, simply not of the fine-material sphere, simply not of the immaterial sphere, simply included in a sphere, simply not outside any sphere, simply unfixed, simply not leading out, simply arisen and knowable by mind-consciousness, simply impermanent, simply overcome by aging.

"The five kinds of consciousness have arisen bases and arisen objects": they arise when the basis has arisen and the object has arisen.
"They have bases arisen before them and objects arisen before them": they arise when the basis has arisen before and the object has arisen before.
"They have internal bases and external objects": the bases of the five kinds of consciousness are internal; their objects are external.
"They have unbroken bases and unbroken objects": they arise when the basis is unbroken and the object is unbroken.
"They have different bases and different objects": the basis and object of eye-consciousness are one thing; the basis and object of ear-consciousness are another; the basis and object of nose-consciousness are another; the basis and object of tongue-consciousness are another; the basis and object of body-consciousness are another.

"They do not experience one another's field and range": ear-consciousness does not experience the field and range of eye-consciousness, nor does eye-consciousness experience the field and range of ear-consciousness. Nose-consciousness does not experience the field and range of eye-consciousness, nor does eye-consciousness experience the field and range of nose-consciousness. Tongue-consciousness does not experience the field and range of eye-consciousness, nor does eye-consciousness experience the field and range of tongue-consciousness. Body-consciousness does not experience the field and range of eye-consciousness, nor does eye-consciousness experience the field and range of body-consciousness. Of ear-consciousness… of nose-consciousness… of tongue-consciousness… eye-consciousness does not experience the field and range of body-consciousness, nor does body-consciousness experience the field and range of eye-consciousness. Ear-consciousness does not experience the field and range of body-consciousness, nor does body-consciousness experience the field and range of ear-consciousness. Nose-consciousness does not experience the field and range of body-consciousness, nor does body-consciousness experience the field and range of nose-consciousness. Tongue-consciousness does not experience the field and range of body-consciousness, nor does body-consciousness experience the field and range of tongue-consciousness.

"They do not arise without bringing-to-mind": they arise for one who brings to mind.
"They do not arise without attention": they arise for one who attends.
"They do not arise uninterruptedly": they do not arise in unbroken succession.
"They do not arise not-before and not-after": they do not arise at a single moment.

"They do not arise in immediate succession to one another": ear-consciousness does not arise in immediate succession to the arising of eye-consciousness, nor does eye-consciousness arise in immediate succession to the arising of ear-consciousness. Nose-consciousness does not arise in immediate succession to the arising of eye-consciousness, nor does eye-consciousness arise in immediate succession to the arising of nose-consciousness. Tongue-consciousness does not arise in immediate succession to the arising of eye-consciousness, nor does eye-consciousness arise in immediate succession to the arising of tongue-consciousness. Body-consciousness does not arise in immediate succession to the arising of eye-consciousness, nor does eye-consciousness arise in immediate succession to the arising of body-consciousness. Of ear-consciousness… of nose-consciousness… of tongue-consciousness… eye-consciousness does not arise in immediate succession to the arising of body-consciousness, nor does body-consciousness arise in immediate succession to the arising of eye-consciousness. Ear-consciousness does not arise in immediate succession to the arising of body-consciousness, nor does body-consciousness arise in immediate succession to the arising of ear-consciousness. Nose-consciousness does not arise in immediate succession to the arising of body-consciousness, nor does body-consciousness arise in immediate succession to the arising of nose-consciousness. Tongue-consciousness does not arise in immediate succession to the arising of body-consciousness, nor does body-consciousness arise in immediate succession to the arising of tongue-consciousness.

"The five kinds of consciousness are without engagement": for the five kinds of consciousness there is no turning towards, no engagement, no bringing-to-mind, no attention.
"By the five kinds of consciousness one does not cognise any thing": by the five kinds of consciousness one does not cognise any thing.
"Except as a mere falling upon": except as a mere coming into range.
"Even in immediate succession to the five kinds of consciousness one does not cognise any thing": even by the mind element in immediate succession to the five kinds of consciousness one does not cognise any thing.
"By the five kinds of consciousness one does not adopt any posture": by the five kinds of consciousness one does not adopt any posture — walking, standing, sitting, or lying down.
"Even in immediate succession to the five kinds of consciousness one does not adopt any posture": even by the mind element in immediate succession to the five kinds of consciousness one does not adopt any posture — walking, standing, sitting, or lying down.
"By the five kinds of consciousness one does not undertake bodily action or verbal action": by the five kinds of consciousness one does not undertake bodily action or verbal action.
"Even in immediate succession to the five kinds of consciousness one does not undertake bodily action or verbal action": even by the mind element in immediate succession to the five kinds of consciousness one does not undertake bodily action or verbal action.
"By the five kinds of consciousness one does not take up a wholesome or unwholesome thing": by the five kinds of consciousness one does not take up a wholesome or unwholesome thing.
"Even in immediate succession to the five kinds of consciousness one does not take up a wholesome or unwholesome thing": even by the mind element in immediate succession to the five kinds of consciousness one does not take up a wholesome or unwholesome thing.
"By the five kinds of consciousness one does not enter an attainment or emerge from it": by the five kinds of consciousness one does not enter an attainment or emerge from it.
"Even in immediate succession to the five kinds of consciousness one does not enter an attainment or emerge from it": even by the mind element in immediate succession to the five kinds of consciousness one does not enter an attainment or emerge from it.
"By the five kinds of consciousness one does not pass away or get reborn": by the five kinds of consciousness one does not pass away or get reborn.
"Even in immediate succession to the five kinds of consciousness one does not pass away or get reborn": even by the mind element in immediate succession to the five kinds of consciousness one does not pass away or get reborn.
"By the five kinds of consciousness one does not sleep, wake, or dream": by the five kinds of consciousness one does not sleep, wake, or dream.
"Even in immediate succession to the five kinds of consciousness one does not sleep, wake, or dream": even by the mind element in immediate succession to the five kinds of consciousness one does not sleep, wake, or dream. Thus there is the wisdom that makes the bases plain as they really are.
Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of one.
The Ones.
The Exposition of the Twos

(1) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is worldly wisdom; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom beyond the world.
(2) All wisdom can be known by one means and cannot be known by another.
(3) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom subject to mental taints; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom without mental taints.
(4) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom dissociated from mental taints but subject to them; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom dissociated from mental taints and without them.
(5) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom that can be bound by fetters; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom that cannot be bound by fetters.
(6) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom dissociated from fetters but able to be bound by them; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom dissociated from fetters and not able to be bound by them.
(7) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom that can be bound by ties; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom that cannot be bound by ties.
(8) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom dissociated from ties but able to be bound by them; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom dissociated from ties and not able to be bound by them.
(9) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom that can be swept by floods; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom that cannot be swept by floods.
(10) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom dissociated from floods but able to be swept by them; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom dissociated from floods and not able to be swept by them.
(11) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom that can be bound by yokes; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom that cannot be bound by yokes.
(12) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom dissociated from yokes but able to be bound by them; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom dissociated from yokes and not able to be bound by them.
(13) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom that can be obstructed by hindrances; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom that cannot be obstructed by hindrances.
(14) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom dissociated from hindrances but able to be obstructed by them; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom dissociated from hindrances and not able to be obstructed by them.
(15) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom that can be wrongly grasped; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom that cannot be wrongly grasped.
(16) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom dissociated from wrong grasping but able to be wrongly grasped; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom dissociated from wrong grasping and not able to be wrongly grasped.
(17) Wisdom in the results of the three planes is wisdom taken up at birth; wisdom in the wholesome of the three planes, in the functional neutral of the three planes, and in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom not taken up at birth.
(18) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom that can be clung to; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom that cannot be clung to.
(19) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom dissociated from clinging but able to be clung to; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom dissociated from clinging and not able to be clung to.
(20) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom connected with defilement; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom not connected with defilement.
(21) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom dissociated from defilements but connected with defilement; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom dissociated from defilements and not connected with defilement.
(22) Wisdom associated with thought is wisdom with thought; wisdom dissociated from thought is wisdom without thought.
(23) Wisdom associated with examination is wisdom with examination; wisdom dissociated from examination is wisdom without examination.
(24) Wisdom associated with joy is wisdom with joy; wisdom dissociated from joy is wisdom without joy.
(25) Wisdom associated with joy is wisdom accompanied by joy; wisdom dissociated from joy is wisdom not accompanied by joy.
(26) Wisdom associated with happiness is wisdom accompanied by happiness; wisdom dissociated from happiness is wisdom not accompanied by happiness.
(27) Wisdom associated with equanimity is wisdom accompanied by equanimity; wisdom dissociated from equanimity is wisdom not accompanied by equanimity.
(28) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the sense sphere is wisdom of the sense sphere; wisdom of the fine-material sphere, wisdom of the immaterial sphere, and wisdom not included in any sphere are wisdom not of the sense sphere.
(29) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the fine-material sphere is wisdom of the fine-material sphere; wisdom of the sense sphere, wisdom of the immaterial sphere, and wisdom not included in any sphere are wisdom not of the fine-material sphere.
(30) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the immaterial sphere is wisdom of the immaterial sphere; wisdom of the sense sphere, wisdom of the fine-material sphere, and wisdom not included in any sphere are wisdom not of the immaterial sphere.
(31) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is wisdom included in a sphere; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom not included in any sphere.
(32) Wisdom in the four paths is wisdom that leads out; wisdom in the wholesome of the three planes, in the results of the four planes, and in the functional neutral of the three planes is wisdom that does not lead out.
(33) Wisdom in the four paths is fixed wisdom; wisdom in the wholesome of the three planes, in the results of the four planes, and in the functional neutral of the three planes is unfixed wisdom.
(34) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the three planes is surpassable wisdom; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is unsurpassed wisdom.
(35) Therein, what is wisdom that brings about a goal?
Wisdom in the wholesome of the four planes, and in the functional neutral of an arahant producing a direct knowledge or producing an attainment, is wisdom that brings about a goal; wisdom in the results of the four planes, and in the functional neutral of an arahant when the direct knowledge has been produced and the attainment has been produced, is wisdom whose goal has been brought about.
Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of two.
The Twos.
The Exposition of the Threes

(1a) Therein, what is wisdom made of reflection? In the fields of work arranged with skill, or the fields of craft arranged with skill, or the branches of science arranged with skill, whether concerning ownership of action or in conformity with the truths — "material form is impermanent", or "feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is impermanent" — whatever conforming acceptance, view, preference, understanding, consideration, acceptance upon reflection on things of such a kind one obtains without hearing it from another: this is called "wisdom made of reflection".
(1b) Therein, what is wisdom made of learning? In the fields of work arranged with skill, or the fields of craft arranged with skill, or the branches of science arranged with skill, whether concerning ownership of action or in conformity with the truths — "material form is impermanent", or "feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is impermanent" — whatever conforming acceptance, view, preference, understanding, consideration, acceptance upon reflection on things of such a kind one obtains by hearing it from another: this is called "wisdom made of learning".
(1c) All wisdom of one who has entered an attainment is wisdom made of meditative development.

(2a) Therein, what is wisdom made of giving? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning giving, in relation to giving: this is called "wisdom made of giving".
(2b) Therein, what is wisdom made of virtue? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning virtue, in relation to virtue: this is called "wisdom made of virtue".
(2c) All wisdom of one who has entered an attainment is wisdom made of meditative development.

(3a) Therein, what is wisdom concerning higher virtue? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one restraining himself with the restraint of the monastic code: this is called "wisdom concerning higher virtue".
(3b) Therein, what is wisdom concerning the higher mind? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one entering a fine-material-sphere or immaterial-sphere attainment: this is called "wisdom concerning the higher mind".
(3c) Therein, what is wisdom concerning higher wisdom? Wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits: this is called "wisdom concerning higher wisdom".

(4a) Therein, what is skill in gain? "When attending to these things, unwholesome things not yet arisen do not arise, and unwholesome things that have arisen are abandoned. Or, when attending to these things, wholesome things not yet arisen arise, and wholesome things that have arisen lead to increase, expansion, development, and perfection" — the wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein: this is called "skill in gain".
(4b) Therein, what is skill in loss? "When attending to these things, wholesome things not yet arisen do not arise, and wholesome things that have arisen cease. Or, when attending to these things, unwholesome things not yet arisen arise, and unwholesome things that have arisen lead to increase and expansion" — the wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein: this is called "skill in loss".
(4c) All wisdom about the means in each case is skill in means.

(5a) Wisdom in the results of the four planes is wisdom that is a result.
(5b) Wisdom in the wholesome of the four planes is wisdom that is a thing subject to result.
(5c) Wisdom in the functional neutral of the three planes is wisdom that is neither a result nor a thing subject to result.

(6a) Wisdom in the results of the three planes is wisdom taken up at birth and able to be clung to.
(6b) Wisdom in the wholesome of the three planes and in the functional neutral of the three planes is wisdom not taken up at birth but able to be clung to.
(6c) Wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom not taken up at birth and not able to be clung to.

(7a) Wisdom associated with thought and examination is wisdom with thought and with examination.
(7b) Wisdom dissociated from thought but associated with examination is wisdom without thought but with examination only.
(7c) Wisdom dissociated from thought and examination is wisdom without thought and without examination.

(8a) Wisdom associated with joy is wisdom accompanied by joy.
(8b) Wisdom associated with happiness is wisdom accompanied by happiness.
(8c) Wisdom associated with equanimity is wisdom accompanied by equanimity.

(9a) Wisdom in the wholesome of the three planes is wisdom leading to accumulation.
(9b) Wisdom in the four paths is wisdom leading to dismantling.
(9c) Wisdom in the results of the four planes and in the functional neutral of the three planes is wisdom leading neither to accumulation nor to dismantling.

(10a) Wisdom in the four paths and in three fruits is wisdom of one in training.
(10b) Wisdom in the highest fruit, the fruit of arahantship, is wisdom of one beyond training.
(10c) Wisdom in the wholesome of the three planes, in the results of the three planes, and in the functional neutral of the three planes is wisdom of one neither in training nor beyond training.

(11a) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the sense sphere is limited wisdom.
(11b) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the fine-material and immaterial spheres is expanded wisdom.
(11c) Wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is measureless wisdom.

(12a) Therein, what is wisdom with a limited object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning limited things: this is called "wisdom with a limited object".

(12b) Therein, what is wisdom with an expanded object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning expanded things: this is called "wisdom with an expanded object".

(12c) Therein, what is wisdom with a measureless object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning measureless things: this is called "wisdom with a measureless object".

(13a) Therein, what is wisdom with the path as its object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning the noble path: this is called "wisdom with the path as its object".
(13b) Wisdom in the four paths is wisdom with the path as its cause.

(13c) Therein, what is wisdom with the path as its dominant factor? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises making the noble path the dominant factor: this is called "wisdom with the path as its dominant factor".

(14) Wisdom in the results of the four planes may be arisen, may be due to arise; it is not describable as unarisen. Wisdom in the wholesome of the four planes and in the functional neutral of the three planes may be arisen, may be unarisen; it is not describable as due to arise.
(15) All wisdom may be past, may be future, may be present.

(16a) Therein, what is wisdom with a past object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning past things: this is called "wisdom with a past object".

(16b) Therein, what is wisdom with a future object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning future things: this is called "wisdom with a future object".

(16c) Therein, what is wisdom with a present object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning present things: this is called "wisdom with a present object".
(17) All wisdom may be internal, may be external, may be both internal and external.

(18a) Therein, what is wisdom with an internal object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning internal things: this is called "wisdom with an internal object".

(18b) Therein, what is wisdom with an external object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning external things: this is called "wisdom with an external object".

(18c) Therein, what is wisdom with both an internal and external object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning things both internal and external: this is called "wisdom with both an internal and external object".
Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of three.
The Threes.
The Exposition of the Fours

(1a) Therein, what is knowledge that action is one's own? "There is what is given, there is what is offered, there is what is sacrificed; there is the fruit and result of well-done and badly-done actions; there is this world, there is the other world; there is mother, there is father; there are spontaneously reborn beings; there are in the world ascetics and brahmins of right conduct and right practice who declare this world and the other world, having realised them for themselves by direct knowledge" — the wisdom of such a kind, the understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view: this is called "knowledge that action is one's own". Setting aside knowledge in conformity with the truths, all wholesome wisdom that is subject to mental taints is knowledge that action is one's own.
(1b) Therein, what is knowledge in conformity with the truths? "Material form is impermanent", or "feeling… perception… formations… consciousness is impermanent" — whatever conforming acceptance, view, preference, understanding, consideration, acceptance upon reflection on things of such a kind: this is called "knowledge in conformity with the truths".
(1c) Wisdom in the four paths is the knowledge of one endowed with the path.
(1d) Wisdom in the four fruits is the knowledge of one endowed with the fruit.

(2) The knowledge of one endowed with the path is knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the cessation of suffering, and knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of suffering.
(a) Therein, what is knowledge of suffering? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning suffering: this is called "knowledge of suffering".
(b–d) Concerning the origin of suffering… concerning the cessation of suffering… concerning the way leading to the cessation of suffering, the wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises: this is called "knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of suffering".

(3) Wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the sense sphere is wisdom of the sense sphere; wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the fine-material sphere is wisdom of the fine-material sphere; wisdom in the wholesome and neutral of the immaterial sphere is wisdom of the immaterial sphere; wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is wisdom not included in any sphere.

(4a) Therein, what is knowledge of the teaching? Wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits is knowledge of the teaching.
(4b) By this teaching that is known, seen, reached, understood, and fathomed, he draws the inference concerning past and future: "Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the past directly knew suffering, directly knew the origin of suffering, directly knew the cessation of suffering, directly knew the way leading to the cessation of suffering, it was just this suffering they directly knew, just this origin of suffering they directly knew, just this cessation of suffering they directly knew, just this way leading to the cessation of suffering they directly knew. Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the future will directly know suffering, will directly know the origin of suffering, will directly know the cessation of suffering, will directly know the way leading to the cessation of suffering, it is just this suffering they will directly know, just this origin of suffering they will directly know, just this cessation of suffering they will directly know, just this way leading to the cessation of suffering they will directly know" — the wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein: this is called "inferential knowledge".
(4c) Therein, what is knowledge of encompassing others' minds? Here a monk knows the minds of other beings, of other persons, having encompassed them with his own mind. He knows a mind with lust as "a mind with lust"; he knows a mind without lust as "a mind without lust"; he knows a mind with hate as "a mind with hate"; he knows a mind without hate as "a mind without hate"; he knows a mind with delusion as "a mind with delusion"; he knows a mind without delusion as "a mind without delusion"; he knows a contracted mind as "a contracted mind"; he knows a distracted mind as "a distracted mind"; he knows an expanded mind as "an expanded mind"; he knows an unexpanded mind as "an unexpanded mind"; he knows a surpassable mind as "a surpassable mind"; he knows an unsurpassable mind as "an unsurpassable mind"; he knows a concentrated mind as "a concentrated mind"; he knows an unconcentrated mind as "an unconcentrated mind"; he knows a freed mind as "a freed mind"; he knows an unfreed mind as "an unfreed mind" — the wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein: this is called "knowledge of encompassing others' minds".
(4d) Setting aside knowledge of the teaching, inferential knowledge, and knowledge of encompassing others' minds, the remaining wisdom is conventional knowledge.

(5a) Therein, what is wisdom for accumulation and not for dismantling? Wisdom in the wholesome of the sense sphere is for accumulation and not for dismantling.
(5b) Wisdom in the four paths is for dismantling and not for accumulation.
(5c) Wisdom in the wholesome of the fine-material and immaterial spheres is both for accumulation and for dismantling.
(5d) The remaining wisdom is neither for accumulation nor for dismantling.

(6a) Therein, what is wisdom for disenchantment and not for penetration? The wisdom by which one becomes dispassionate towards sense pleasures, but does not penetrate the direct knowledges or the truths: this is called "wisdom for disenchantment and not for penetration".
(6b) Being already dispassionate towards sense pleasures by that wisdom, one penetrates the direct knowledges but not the truths: this is called "wisdom for penetration and not for disenchantment".
(6c) Wisdom in the four paths is both for disenchantment and for penetration.
(6d) The remaining wisdom is neither for disenchantment nor for penetration.

(7a) Therein, what is wisdom that shares in decline? When perceptions and attentions accompanied by sense pleasure beset one who has gained the first meditative absorption, that is wisdom that shares in decline.
(7b) When mindfulness in conformity with that state stands firm, that is wisdom that shares in stability.
(7c) When perceptions and attentions accompanied by absence of thought beset him, that is wisdom that shares in distinction.
(7d) When perceptions and attentions accompanied by disenchantment, connected with dispassion, beset him, that is wisdom that shares in breaking through. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by thought beset one who has gained the second meditative absorption, that is wisdom that shares in decline. When mindfulness in conformity with that state stands firm, that is wisdom that shares in stability. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by equanimity beset him, that is wisdom that shares in distinction. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by disenchantment, connected with dispassion, beset him, that is wisdom that shares in breaking through. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by joy and happiness beset one who has gained the third meditative absorption, that is wisdom that shares in decline. When mindfulness in conformity with that state stands firm, that is wisdom that shares in stability. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by neither-pain-nor-pleasure beset him, that is wisdom that shares in distinction. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by disenchantment, connected with dispassion, beset him, that is wisdom that shares in breaking through. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by equanimity beset one who has gained the fourth meditative absorption, that is wisdom that shares in decline. When mindfulness in conformity with that state stands firm, that is wisdom that shares in stability. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by the field of infinite space beset him, that is wisdom that shares in distinction. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by disenchantment, connected with dispassion, beset him, that is wisdom that shares in breaking through. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by material form beset one who has gained the field of infinite space, that is wisdom that shares in decline. When mindfulness in conformity with that state stands firm, that is wisdom that shares in stability. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by the field of infinite consciousness beset him, that is wisdom that shares in distinction. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by disenchantment, connected with dispassion, beset him, that is wisdom that shares in breaking through. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by the field of infinite space beset one who has gained the field of infinite consciousness, that is wisdom that shares in decline. When mindfulness in conformity with that state stands firm, that is wisdom that shares in stability. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by the field of nothingness beset him, that is wisdom that shares in distinction. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by disenchantment, connected with dispassion, beset him, that is wisdom that shares in breaking through. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by the field of infinite consciousness beset one who has gained the field of nothingness, that is wisdom that shares in decline. When mindfulness in conformity with that state stands firm, that is wisdom that shares in stability. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception beset him, that is wisdom that shares in distinction. When perceptions and attentions accompanied by disenchantment, connected with dispassion, beset him, that is wisdom that shares in breaking through.

(8) Therein, what are the four analytical knowledges? The analytical knowledge of meaning, the analytical knowledge of principles, the analytical knowledge of language, the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. Knowledge with regard to meaning is the analytical knowledge of meaning; knowledge with regard to principles is the analytical knowledge of principles; knowledge with regard to the expression of the language of those principles is the analytical knowledge of language; knowledge with regard to knowledges is the analytical knowledge of ready understanding. These are the four analytical knowledges.

(9) Therein, what are the four modes of practice? Wisdom of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge, wisdom of difficult practice and quick direct knowledge, wisdom of easy practice and slow direct knowledge, wisdom of easy practice and quick direct knowledge.
(a) Therein, what is wisdom of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one producing concentration with trouble and difficulty and knowing that state slowly: this is called "wisdom of difficult practice and slow direct knowledge".
(b) Therein, what is wisdom of difficult practice and quick direct knowledge? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one producing concentration with trouble and difficulty and knowing that state quickly: this is called "wisdom of difficult practice and quick direct knowledge".
(c) Therein, what is wisdom of easy practice and slow direct knowledge? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one producing concentration without trouble and without difficulty and knowing that state slowly: this is called "wisdom of easy practice and slow direct knowledge".
(d) Therein, what is wisdom of easy practice and quick direct knowledge? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one producing concentration without trouble and without difficulty and knowing that state quickly: this is called "wisdom of easy practice and quick direct knowledge". These are the four modes of practice.

(10) Therein, what are the four objects? Limited wisdom with a limited object, limited wisdom with a measureless object, measureless wisdom with a limited object, measureless wisdom with a measureless object.
(a) Therein, what is limited wisdom with a limited object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one who has not fully mastered concentration and who pervades a small object: this is called "limited wisdom with a limited object".
(b) Therein, what is limited wisdom with a measureless object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one who has not fully mastered concentration and who pervades a vast object: this is called "limited wisdom with a measureless object".
(c) Therein, what is measureless wisdom with a limited object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one who has fully mastered concentration and who pervades a small object: this is called "measureless wisdom with a limited object".
(d) Therein, what is measureless wisdom with a measureless object? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises in one who has fully mastered concentration and who pervades a vast object: this is called "measureless wisdom with a measureless object". These are the four objects.
(11) The knowledge of one endowed with the path is knowledge of aging and death, knowledge of the origin of aging and death, knowledge of the cessation of aging and death, and knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of aging and death.
(a) Therein, what is knowledge of aging and death? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning aging and death: this is called "knowledge of aging and death".
(b–d) Concerning the origin of aging and death… concerning the cessation of aging and death… concerning the way leading to the cessation of aging and death, the wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises: this is called "knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of aging and death".

(12-21) The knowledge of one endowed with the teaching is knowledge of birth… knowledge of existence… knowledge of clinging… knowledge of craving… knowledge of feeling… knowledge of contact… knowledge of the six sense-fields… knowledge of mentality and material form… knowledge of consciousness… knowledge of formations, knowledge of the origin of formations, knowledge of the cessation of formations, knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of formations.
Therein, what is knowledge of formations? The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises concerning formations: this is called "knowledge of formations".
Concerning the origin of formations… concerning the cessation of formations… concerning the way leading to the cessation of formations, the wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view that arises: this is called "knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of formations. Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of four.
The Fours.
The Exposition of the Fives

(1) Therein, what is five-factored right concentration? The pervasion with joy, the pervasion with happiness, the pervasion with mind, the pervasion with light, and the sign for reviewing. Wisdom in two meditative absorptions is the pervasion with joy. Wisdom in three meditative absorptions is the pervasion with happiness. Knowledge of others' minds is the pervasion with mind. The divine eye is the pervasion with light. The reviewing knowledge of one who has emerged from this or that concentration is the sign for reviewing. This is called five-factored right concentration.
(2) Therein, what is five-knowledged right concentration? The knowledge arises in oneself: "This concentration is both pleasant now and pleasant in its result in the future." The knowledge arises in oneself: "This concentration is noble and unworldly." The knowledge arises in oneself: "This concentration is not practised by base people." The knowledge arises in oneself: "This concentration is peaceful, refined, obtained by tranquillisation, attained through unification, and not maintained by forceful suppression with effort." The knowledge arises in oneself: "Mindful I enter this concentration, and mindful I emerge from it." This is five-knowledged right concentration. Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of five.
The Fives.
The Exposition of the Sixes

Therein, what is wisdom in the six direct knowledges? Knowledge of the kinds of supernormal power, knowledge of the purification of the ear element, knowledge of others' minds, knowledge of the recollection of past lives, knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings, knowledge of the destruction of the mental taints — this is wisdom in the six direct knowledges. Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of six.
The Sixes.
The Exposition of the Sevens

Therein, what are the seventy-seven grounds of knowledge? Knowledge that with birth as condition there is aging and death; knowledge that when there is no birth there is no aging and death; knowledge that in the past too, with birth as condition, there was aging and death; knowledge that when there was no birth there was no aging and death; knowledge that in the future too, with birth as condition, there will be aging and death; knowledge that when there is no birth there will be no aging and death. And the knowledge that this knowledge of the fixity of things is itself subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, subject to cessation. Knowledge that with existence as condition there is birth… knowledge that with clinging as condition there is existence… knowledge that with craving as condition there is clinging… knowledge that with feeling as condition there is craving… knowledge that with contact as condition there is feeling… knowledge that with the six sense-fields as condition there is contact… knowledge that with mentality and material form as condition there are the six sense-fields… knowledge that with consciousness as condition there is mentality and material form… knowledge that with formations as condition there is consciousness… knowledge that with ignorance as condition there are formations; knowledge that when there is no ignorance there are no formations; knowledge that in the past too, with ignorance as condition, there were formations; knowledge that when there was no ignorance there were no formations; knowledge that in the future too, with ignorance as condition, there will be formations; knowledge that when there is no ignorance there will be no formations. And the knowledge that this knowledge of the fixity of things is itself subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, subject to cessation. These are the seventy-seven grounds of knowledge. Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of seven.
The Sevens.
The Exposition of the Eights

Therein, what is wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits? Wisdom in the path of stream-entry, wisdom in the fruit of stream-entry, wisdom in the path of once-returning, wisdom in the fruit of once-returning, wisdom in the path of non-returning, wisdom in the fruit of non-returning, wisdom in the path of arahantship, wisdom in the fruit of arahantship — this is wisdom in the four paths and the four fruits. Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of eight.
The Eights.
The Exposition of the Nines

Therein, what is wisdom in the nine successive dwelling attainments? Wisdom in the attainment of the first meditative absorption, wisdom in the attainment of the second meditative absorption, wisdom in the attainment of the third meditative absorption, wisdom in the attainment of the fourth meditative absorption, wisdom in the attainment of the field of infinite space, wisdom in the attainment of the field of infinite consciousness, wisdom in the attainment of the field of nothingness, wisdom in the attainment of the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and the reviewing knowledge of one who has emerged from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling — this is wisdom in the nine successive dwelling attainments. Thus is the ground of knowledge by way of nine.
The Nines.
The Exposition of the Tens

(1) Therein, what is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the possible as possible and the impossible as impossible? Here the Tathāgata knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a person accomplished in view should take any formation as permanent — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that an ordinary person should take some formation as permanent — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a person accomplished in view should take any formation as pleasant — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that an ordinary person should take some formation as pleasant — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a person accomplished in view should take any thing as self — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that an ordinary person should take some thing as self — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a person accomplished in view should deprive his mother of life — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that an ordinary person should deprive his mother of life — this is possible."
He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a person accomplished in view should deprive his father of life… should deprive an arahant of life… should with a mind of hatred shed the blood of a Tathāgata… should split the Order… should acknowledge another teacher… should produce an eighth existence — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that an ordinary person should produce an eighth existence — this is possible."
He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that two arahants who are fully awakened Buddhas should arise in one world system neither before nor after each other — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that one arahant who is a fully awakened Buddha should arise in one world system — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that two wheel-turning kings should arise in one world system neither before nor after each other — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that one wheel-turning king should arise in one world system — this is possible."
He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a woman should be an arahant who is a fully awakened Buddha — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that a man should be an arahant who is a fully awakened Buddha — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a woman should be a wheel-turning king — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that a man should be a wheel-turning king — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a woman should exercise the rulership of Sakka, the rulership of Māra, the rulership of Brahmā — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that a man should exercise the rulership of Sakka, the rulership of Māra, the rulership of Brahmā — this is possible."
He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a wished-for, desired, agreeable result should come from bodily misconduct — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that an unwished-for, undesired, disagreeable result should come from bodily misconduct — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that a wished-for, desired, agreeable result should come from verbal misconduct… from mental misconduct — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that an unwished-for, undesired, disagreeable result should come from verbal misconduct… from mental misconduct — this is possible."
He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that an unwished-for, undesired, disagreeable result should come from good bodily conduct — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that a wished-for, desired, agreeable result should come from good bodily conduct — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that an unwished-for, undesired, disagreeable result should come from good verbal conduct… from good mental conduct — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that a wished-for, desired, agreeable result should come from good verbal conduct… from good mental conduct — this is possible."
He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that one given to bodily misconduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that one given to bodily misconduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, hell — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that one given to verbal misconduct… one given to mental misconduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that one given to verbal misconduct… one given to mental misconduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, hell — this is possible."
He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that one given to good bodily conduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, hell — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that one given to good bodily conduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world — this is possible." He knows: "It is impossible, it cannot happen, that one given to good verbal conduct… one given to good mental conduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, hell — this is not possible." He knows: "But it is possible that one given to good verbal conduct… one given to good mental conduct should, on that account and because of that, with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world — this is possible." "Whatever things are causes and conditions of whatever things — that, accordingly, is the possible; whatever things are not causes and not conditions of whatever things — that, accordingly, is the impossible." The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein — this is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the possible as possible and the impossible as impossible.

(2) Therein, what is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the result of past, future, and present undertakings of action, according to circumstance and according to cause? Here the Tathāgata knows: "There are some evil undertakings of action which, blocked by a fortunate destination, do not ripen. There are some evil undertakings of action which, blocked by a fortunate body, do not ripen. There are some evil undertakings of action which, blocked by fortunate time, do not ripen. There are some evil undertakings of action which, blocked by fortunate effort, do not ripen.
"There are some evil undertakings of action which ripen through an unfortunate destination. There are some evil undertakings of action which ripen through an unfortunate body. There are some evil undertakings of action which ripen through unfortunate time. There are some evil undertakings of action which ripen through unfortunate effort.
"There are some good undertakings of action which, blocked by an unfortunate destination, do not ripen. There are some good undertakings of action which, blocked by an unfortunate body, do not ripen. There are some good undertakings of action which, blocked by unfortunate time, do not ripen. There are some good undertakings of action which, blocked by unfortunate effort, do not ripen.
"There are some good undertakings of action which ripen through a fortunate destination. There are some good undertakings of action which ripen through a fortunate body. There are some good undertakings of action which ripen through fortunate time. There are some good undertakings of action which ripen through fortunate effort." The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein — this is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the result of past, future, and present undertakings of action, according to circumstance and according to cause.

(3) Therein, what is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the way that leads everywhere? Here the Tathāgata knows: "This is the path, this is the way that leads to hell"; he knows: "This is the path, this is the way that leads to the animal womb"; he knows: "This is the path, this is the way that leads to the realm of ghosts"; he knows: "This is the path, this is the way that leads to the human world"; he knows: "This is the path, this is the way that leads to the world of the gods"; he knows: "This is the path, this is the way that leads to Nibbāna." The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein — this is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the way that leads everywhere.

(4) Therein, what is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the world with its many and different elements? Here the Tathāgata knows the diversity of the aggregates, knows the diversity of the sense-fields, knows the diversity of the elements, knows the diversity of the world with its many and different elements. The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein — this is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the world with its many and different elements.

(5) Therein, what is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the different inclinations of beings? Here the Tathāgata knows: "There are beings of inferior inclination; there are beings of refined inclination. Beings of inferior inclination resort to, frequent, and attend upon beings of inferior inclination. Beings of refined inclination resort to, frequent, and attend upon beings of refined inclination.
"In the past too, beings of inferior inclination resorted to, frequented, and attended upon beings of inferior inclination; beings of refined inclination resorted to, frequented, and attended upon beings of refined inclination.
"In the future too, beings of inferior inclination will resort to, frequent, and attend upon beings of inferior inclination; beings of refined inclination will resort to, frequent, and attend upon beings of refined inclination." The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein — this is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the different inclinations of beings.

(6) Therein, what is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the higher and lower state of the faculties of other beings, of other persons? Here the Tathāgata knows the disposition of beings, knows their underlying tendencies, knows their conduct, knows their inclination; he knows beings with little dust in their eyes and much dust in their eyes, with sharp faculties and dull faculties, of good character and bad character, easy to instruct and hard to instruct, capable and incapable.

And what is the disposition of beings? "The world is eternal", or "the world is not eternal", or "the world is finite", or "the world is infinite", or "the soul and the body are the same", or "the soul is one thing and the body another", or "a Tathāgata exists after death", or "a Tathāgata does not exist after death", or "a Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death", or "a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death" — thus beings rely either on the view of existence or on the view of non-existence. Or, avoiding both these extremes, they have gained the conforming acceptance with regard to things that are dependently arisen through specific conditionality, and the knowledge of them as they really are. This is the disposition of beings.

And what are the underlying tendencies of beings? There are seven underlying tendencies: the underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to lust for existence, the underlying tendency to ignorance. Whatever in the world is a dear and agreeable form — there the underlying tendency of beings to lust lies latent. Whatever in the world is a disagreeable and unpleasant form — there the underlying tendency of beings to aversion lies latent. So ignorance lies fallen upon these two things; and conceit, views, and doubt, standing together with it, should be seen there too. This is the underlying tendency of beings.
And what is the conduct of beings? The meritorious formation, the demeritorious formation, the imperturbable formation, whether on a limited plane or on a great plane — this is the conduct of beings.

And what is the inclination of beings? There are beings of inferior inclination; there are beings of refined inclination. Beings of inferior inclination resort to, frequent, and attend upon beings of inferior inclination. Beings of refined inclination resort to, frequent, and attend upon beings of refined inclination.
In the past too, beings of inferior inclination resorted to, frequented, and attended upon beings of inferior inclination; beings of refined inclination resorted to, frequented, and attended upon beings of refined inclination.
In the future too, beings of inferior inclination will resort to, frequent, and attend upon beings of inferior inclination; beings of refined inclination will resort to, frequent, and attend upon beings of refined inclination. This is the inclination of beings.

Which beings have much dust in their eyes? The ten grounds of defilement: greed, hate, delusion, conceit, views, doubt, dullness, restlessness, shamelessness, lack of moral dread. Those beings by whom these ten grounds of defilement have been practised, developed, cultivated, and heaped up — these are the beings with much dust in their eyes.

Which beings have little dust in their eyes? Those beings by whom these ten grounds of defilement have not been practised, not developed, not cultivated, and not heaped up — these are the beings with little dust in their eyes.

Which beings have dull faculties? The five faculties: the faculty of confidence, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom. Those beings by whom these five faculties have not been practised, not developed, not cultivated, and not heaped up — these are the beings with dull faculties.
Which beings have sharp faculties? Those beings by whom these five faculties have been practised, developed, cultivated, and heaped up — these are the beings with sharp faculties.

Which beings are of bad character? Those beings who have evil dispositions, evil underlying tendencies, evil conduct, and evil inclinations, with much dust in their eyes and dull faculties — these are the beings of bad character.

Which beings are of good character? Those beings who have good dispositions, good conduct, and good inclinations, with little dust in their eyes and sharp faculties — these are the beings of good character.
Which beings are hard to instruct? Those beings who are of bad character are the very beings hard to instruct. And those beings who are of good character are the very beings easy to instruct.

Which beings are incapable? Those beings who possess the obstruction of action, possess the obstruction of defilement, possess the obstruction of result, who are without confidence, without desire, and without wisdom, and are incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness in wholesome things — these are the incapable beings.

Which beings are capable? Those beings who do not possess the obstruction of action, do not possess the obstruction of defilement, do not possess the obstruction of result, who have confidence, desire, and wisdom, and are capable of entering the fixed course of rightness in wholesome things — these are the capable beings. The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein — this is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the higher and lower state of the faculties of other beings, of other persons.

(7) Therein, what is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the defilement, the cleansing, and the emergence in the meditative absorptions, liberations, concentrations, and attainments? "A meditator": there are four meditators. There is one meditator who takes what is truly success to be failure; there is one meditator who takes what is truly failure to be success; there is one meditator who takes what is truly success to be success; there is one meditator who takes what is truly failure to be failure — these are the four meditators.
There are another four meditators. There is one meditator who enters slowly and emerges quickly; there is one meditator who enters quickly and emerges slowly; there is one meditator who enters slowly and emerges slowly; there is one meditator who enters quickly and emerges quickly — these are the four meditators.
There are another four meditators. There is one meditator who is skilled in the concentration within concentration but not skilled in the attainment within concentration; there is one meditator who is skilled in the attainment within concentration but not skilled in the concentration within concentration; there is one meditator who is skilled both in the concentration within concentration and in the attainment within concentration; there is one meditator who is skilled neither in the concentration within concentration nor in the attainment within concentration — these are the four meditators.
"Meditative absorption": there are four meditative absorptions — the first meditative absorption, the second meditative absorption, the third meditative absorption, the fourth meditative absorption.
"Liberation": there are eight liberations. Possessing material form, one sees material forms — this is the first liberation.
Not perceiving material form internally, one sees material forms externally — this is the second liberation.
One is resolved only upon the beautiful — this is the third liberation.
Completely passing beyond perceptions of material form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, not attending to perceptions of diversity, aware that "space is infinite", one enters and dwells in the field of infinite space — this is the fourth liberation.
Completely passing beyond the field of infinite space, aware that "consciousness is infinite", one enters and dwells in the field of infinite consciousness — this is the fifth liberation.
Completely passing beyond the field of infinite consciousness, aware that "there is nothing", one enters and dwells in the field of nothingness — this is the sixth liberation.
Completely passing beyond the field of nothingness, one enters and dwells in the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception — this is the seventh liberation.
Completely passing beyond the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, one enters and dwells in the cessation of perception and feeling — this is the eighth liberation.
"Concentration": there are three concentrations — concentration with thought and with examination, concentration without thought but with examination only, concentration without thought and without examination.
"Attainment": there are nine successive dwelling attainments — the attainment of the first meditative absorption, the attainment of the second meditative absorption, the attainment of the third meditative absorption, the attainment of the fourth meditative absorption, the attainment of the field of infinite space, the attainment of the field of infinite consciousness, the attainment of the field of nothingness, the attainment of the field of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling.
"Defilement": the state that shares in decline. "Cleansing": the state that shares in distinction. "Emergence": cleansing is also emergence; emerging from this or that concentration is also emergence. The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein — this is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the defilement, the cleansing, and the emergence in the meditative absorptions, liberations, concentrations, and attainments.

(8) Therein, what is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the recollection of past lives? Here the Tathāgata recollects his manifold past lives, that is: one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many eons of world-contraction, many eons of world-expansion, many eons of world-contraction and expansion: "There I was so named, of such a clan, of such appearance, with such food, experiencing such happiness and pain, with such a life span; passing away from there, I arose elsewhere; and there too I was so named, of such a clan, of such appearance, with such food, experiencing such happiness and pain, with such a life span; passing away from there, I was reborn here." Thus with its aspects and details he recollects his manifold past lives. The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein — this is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the recollection of past lives.

(9) Therein, what is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the passing away and rebirth of beings? Here the Tathāgata, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, sees beings passing away and being reborn — inferior and refined, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate — and he knows beings faring according to their actions: "These beings, indeed, endowed with bodily misconduct, endowed with verbal misconduct, endowed with mental misconduct, revilers of the noble ones, of wrong view, undertaking action based on wrong view — with the breakup of the body after death they have been reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, hell. But these beings, endowed with good bodily conduct, endowed with good verbal conduct, endowed with good mental conduct, not revilers of the noble ones, of right view, undertaking action based on right view — with the breakup of the body after death they have been reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world." Thus with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, he sees beings passing away and being reborn — inferior and refined, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate — and he knows beings faring according to their actions. The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein — this is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the passing away and rebirth of beings.

(10) Therein, what is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the destruction of the mental taints? Here the Tathāgata, with the destruction of the mental taints, having realised for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, enters and dwells in it. The wisdom, understanding… non-delusion, investigation of things, right view therein — this is the Tathāgata's knowledge, as it really is, of the destruction of the mental taints.
The Tens.
The Analysis of Knowledge is finished.
