The Exposition of the Ones
(1) Intoxication with birth

Therein, what is intoxication with birth? On account of birth: the intoxication, being intoxicated, state of intoxication; the conceit, conceiving, state of conceiving; the loftiness, haughtiness, the banner, arrogance, the mind's desire for a flag — this is called "intoxication with birth".
(2-27) Intoxication with clan and the rest

Therein, what is intoxication with clan? On account of clan… on account of health… on account of youth… on account of life… on account of gain… on account of honour… on account of respect… on account of being put first… on account of one's following… on account of wealth… on account of beauty… on account of learning… on account of quick understanding… on account of seniority… on account of being an alms-goer… on account of not being despised… on account of deportment… on account of success… on account of fame… on account of virtue… on account of meditative absorption… on account of craft… on account of height… on account of build… on account of figure… on account of completeness: the intoxication, being intoxicated, state of intoxication; the conceit, conceiving, state of conceiving; the loftiness, haughtiness, the banner, arrogance, the mind's desire for a flag — this is called "intoxication with completeness".
(28) Intoxication

Therein, what is intoxication? The intoxication, being intoxicated, state of intoxication; the conceit, conceiving, state of conceiving; the loftiness, haughtiness, the banner, arrogance, the mind's desire for a flag — this is called "intoxication".
(29) Heedlessness

Therein, what is heedlessness? Letting the mind loose in bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, or the five strands of sense pleasure, and repeatedly letting it loose; acting without respect for the development of wholesome things, acting without perseverance, acting inconstantly, sluggish behaviour, putting down desire, putting down the responsibility, non-practice, non-development, non-cultivation, non-resolution, non-application, heedlessness; whatever heedlessness of this kind there is, being heedless, the state of heedlessness — this is called "heedlessness".
(30) Obstinacy
Therein, what is obstinacy? The obstinacy, being obstinate, state of obstinacy; hardness, harshness, rigidity of mind, unpliability — this is called "obstinacy".
(31) Contentiousness
Therein, what is contentiousness? The contentiousness, counter-contentiousness, being contentious, being counter-contentious, the state of counter-contentiousness — this is called "contentiousness".
(32) Excessive desire

Therein, what is excessive desire? The wanting of more by one discontented with whatever robes, alms-food, dwelling place, and medicinal supports for the sick he has, or with the five strands of sense pleasure; whatever desire of this kind there is, being desirous, excessive desire, lust, passion, passion of the mind — this is called "excessive desire".
(33) Great desire

Therein, what is great desire? The wanting of more by one discontented with whatever robes, alms-food, dwelling place, and medicinal supports for the sick he has, or with the five strands of sense pleasure; whatever desire of this kind there is, being desirous, great desire, lust, passion, passion of the mind — this is called "great desire".
(34) Evil desire

Therein, what is evil desire? Here someone without confidence wishes, "May people know me as one with confidence"; being of bad conduct, he wishes, "May people know me as virtuous"; being of little learning, he wishes, "May people know me as learned"; delighting in company, he wishes, "May people know me as secluded"; being lazy, he wishes, "May people know me as energetic"; being forgetful, he wishes, "May people know me as one of established mindfulness"; being unconcentrated, he wishes, "May people know me as concentrated"; being without wisdom, he wishes, "May people know me as wise"; not having destroyed the mental taints, he wishes, "May people know me as one who has destroyed the mental taints" — whatever desire of this kind there is, being desirous, evil desire, lust, passion, passion of the mind — this is called "evil desire".
(35) Affectation
Therein, what is affectation? The affectation, being affected, cleverness, artfulness, studied elegance, the state of studied elegance — this is called "affectation".
(36) Greediness

Therein, what is greediness? The greediness, being greedy, the state of greediness; covetousness, being covetous, the state of covetousness; itching desire, the wish for what is nice — this is called "greediness".
(37) Frivolity

Therein, what is frivolity? Adorning the robes, adorning the bowl, adorning the dwelling place, adorning and beautifying this putrid body or one's outward requisites; playing, playing about, delighting, the state of delighting, fickleness, frivolity — this is called "frivolity".
(38) Discordant behaviour

Therein, what is discordant behaviour? Towards mother, or father, or elder brother, or teachers, or preceptor, or the Buddha, or the disciples, or towards any others who stand in the place of respect: contrary grasping, delight in opposition, disrespect, disrespectfulness, lack of reverence, lack of deference — this is called "discordant behaviour".
(39) Discontent

Therein, what is discontent? Discontent with remote dwelling places or with any of the higher wholesome things; being discontented, dissatisfaction, not delighting, restlessness, anxiety — this is called "discontent".
(40) Sloth
Therein, what is sloth? The sloth, being slothful, mental sluggishness; laziness, being lazy, the state of laziness — this is called "sloth".
(41) Stretching oneself

Therein, what is stretching oneself? The stretching of the body, stretching out, bending forward, bending sideways, bending together, bending back, restlessness of body — this is called "stretching oneself".
(42) Drowsiness after meals

Therein, what is drowsiness after meals? The faintness after food of one who has eaten, the weariness after food, the burning after food, the heaviness of the body — this is called "drowsiness after meals".
(43) Sluggishness of mind

Therein, what is sluggishness of mind? The mind's lack of readiness, its unworkableness, its sagging, its slumping; sloth, being slothful, the mind's slothfulness; dullness, being dull, the mind's state of dullness — this is called "sluggishness of mind".
(44) Trickery

Therein, what is trickery? For one relying on gain, honour, and renown, of evil desires, driven by desire: the setting up, arranging, and composing of deportment, the frowning, the frowning look, by what is reckoned as the use of requisites, or by roundabout talk — the trickery, being tricky, the state of trickery — this is called "trickery".
(45) Wheedling talk

Therein, what is wheedling talk? For one relying on gain, honour, and renown, of evil desires, driven by desire: the addressing of others, the talking, the talking along, the talking up, the talking round, the flattering, the excessive flattering, the coaxing, the excessive coaxing, the constant pleasant talk, the fawning, the half-truthful talk, the fondling of children — this is called "wheedling talk".
(46) Hinting

Therein, what is hinting? For one relying on gain, honour, and renown, of evil desires, driven by desire: the sign made to others, the making of signs, the suggestion, the making of suggestions, the roundabout talk, the indirect talk — this is called "hinting".
(47) Belittling

Therein, what is belittling? For one relying on gain, honour, and renown, of evil desires, driven by desire: the abusing of others, the disparaging, the blaming, the deriding, the ridiculing, the mocking, the scoffing, the discrediting, the defaming, the carrying about of criticism, the backbiting — this is called "belittling".
(48) Chasing gain with gain

Therein, what is chasing gain with gain? One relying on gain, honour, and renown, of evil desires, driven by desire, carries goods received here to there, or brings goods received there to here; whatever seeking, seeking out, and seeking around, searching, searching out, and searching around for goods of this kind there is — this is called "chasing gain with gain".
(49) The conceit "I am better"

Therein, what is the conceit "I am better"? Here someone nurses conceit on account of birth, or clan, or good family, or beauty of complexion, or wealth, or study, or field of work, or field of craft, or branch of science, or learning, or quick understanding, or on one ground or another; whatever conceit of this kind there is, conceiving, state of conceiving, loftiness, haughtiness, the banner, arrogance, the mind's desire for a flag — this is called "the conceit 'I am better'".
(50) The conceit "I am equal"

Therein, what is the conceit "I am equal"? Here someone nurses conceit on account of birth, or clan, or good family, or beauty of complexion, or wealth, or study, or field of work, or field of craft, or branch of science, or learning, or quick understanding, or on one ground or another; whatever conceit of this kind there is, conceiving, state of conceiving, loftiness, haughtiness, the banner, arrogance, the mind's desire for a flag — this is called "the conceit 'I am equal'".
(51) The conceit "I am worse"

Therein, what is the conceit "I am worse"? Here someone nurses self-belittling on account of birth, or clan, or good family, or beauty of complexion, or wealth, or study, or field of work, or field of craft, or branch of science, or learning, or quick understanding, or on one ground or another; whatever self-belittling of this kind there is, belittling oneself, the state of belittling oneself, the despising, the looking down, the state of looking down on oneself, self-contempt, self-scorn, self-disparagement — this is called "the conceit 'I am worse'".
(52) The conceit of one who is better, "I am better"

Therein, what is the conceit of one who is better, "I am better"? Here someone is better on account of birth, or clan, or good family, or beauty of complexion, or wealth, or study, or field of work, or field of craft, or branch of science, or learning, or quick understanding, or on one ground or another, and he regards himself as better than others; relying on that, he nurses conceit. Whatever conceit of this kind there is, conceiving, state of conceiving, loftiness, haughtiness, the banner, arrogance, the mind's desire for a flag — this is called "the conceit of one who is better, 'I am better'".

(61) Conceit
Therein, what is conceit? The conceit, conceiving, state of conceiving, loftiness, haughtiness, the banner, arrogance, the mind's desire for a flag — this is called "conceit".
(62) Exaggerated conceit

Therein, what is exaggerated conceit? Here someone despises others on account of birth, or clan, or good family… or on one ground or another. Whatever conceit of this kind there is, conceiving, state of conceiving, loftiness, haughtiness, the banner, arrogance, the mind's desire for a flag — this is called "exaggerated conceit".
(63) Conceit beyond conceit

Therein, what is conceit beyond conceit? Here someone, on account of birth, or clan, or good family… or on one ground or another, at an earlier time regards himself as equal to others, and at a later time regards himself as better. Whatever conceit of this kind there is, conceiving, state of conceiving, loftiness, haughtiness, the banner, arrogance, the mind's desire for a flag — this is called "conceit beyond conceit".
(64) Self-belittling conceit

Therein, what is self-belittling conceit? Here someone nurses self-belittling on account of birth, or clan, or good family, or beauty of complexion, or wealth, or study, or field of work, or field of craft, or branch of science, or learning, or quick understanding, or on one ground or another. Whatever self-belittling of this kind there is, belittling oneself, the state of belittling oneself, the despising, the looking down, the state of looking down on oneself, self-contempt, self-scorn, self-disparagement — this is called "self-belittling conceit".
(65) Over-estimating conceit

Therein, what is over-estimating conceit? Perceiving what has not been reached as reached, perceiving what has not been done as done, perceiving what has not been attained as attained, perceiving what has not been realised as realised; whatever conceit of this kind there is, conceiving, state of conceiving, loftiness, haughtiness, the banner, arrogance, the mind's desire for a flag — this is called "over-estimating conceit".
(66) The conceit "I am"

Therein, what is the conceit "I am"? The conceit "I am" with regard to material form, the desire "I am", the underlying tendency "I am"; with regard to feeling… perception… formations… the conceit "I am" with regard to consciousness, the desire "I am", the underlying tendency "I am"; whatever conceit of this kind there is, conceiving, state of conceiving, loftiness, haughtiness, the banner, arrogance, the mind's desire for a flag — this is called "the conceit 'I am'".
(67) Wrong conceit

Therein, what is wrong conceit? Here someone nurses conceit on account of an evil field of work, or an evil field of craft, or an evil branch of science, or evil learning, or evil quick understanding, or evil virtue, or an evil observance, or evil virtue-and-observance, or an evil view, or on one ground or another; whatever conceit of this kind there is, conceiving, state of conceiving, loftiness, haughtiness, the banner, arrogance, the mind's desire for a flag — this is called "wrong conceit".
(68) Thoughts about relatives
Therein, what are thoughts about relatives? The thinking, thought, wrong intention connected with the household life, concerning relatives — this is called "thoughts about relatives".
(69) Thoughts about one's home country

Therein, what are thoughts about one's home country? The thinking, thought, wrong intention connected with the household life, concerning one's home country — this is called "thoughts about one's home country".
(70) Thoughts about not dying

Therein, what are thoughts about not dying? The thinking, thought, wrong intention connected with the household life, connected either with the practice of austerities or with resort to views — this is called "thoughts about not dying".
(71) Thought connected with sympathy for others

Therein, what is thought connected with sympathy for others? Here someone dwells mixed up with householders, rejoicing with them and sorrowing with them, happy when they are happy, pained when they are pained, and when tasks and duties arise he takes up the effort himself. The thinking, thought, wrong intention connected with the household life therein — this is called "thought connected with sympathy for others".
(72) Thought connected with gain and the rest

Therein, what is thought connected with gain, honour, and renown? The thinking, thought, wrong intention connected with the household life, concerning gain, honour, and renown — this is called "thought connected with gain, honour, and renown".
(73) Thought connected with not being despised

Therein, what is thought connected with not being despised? Here someone thinks, "May others not despise me", on account of birth, or clan, or good family, or beauty of complexion, or wealth, or study, or field of work, or field of craft, or branch of science, or learning, or quick understanding, or on one ground or another. The thinking, thought, wrong intention connected with the household life therein — this is called "thought connected with not being despised".
The Ones.
The Exposition of the Twos
(1) Anger and resentment

(a) Therein, what is anger? The anger, being angry, the state of anger; the hate, hating, state of hating; the malice, being malicious, state of being malicious; the opposition, hostility, fierceness, rudeness, the mind's dissatisfaction — this is called "anger".
(b) Therein, what is resentment? First there is anger, afterwards resentment. Whatever resentment of this kind there is, resenting, the state of resentment; the keeping up, maintaining, and fixing of anger, its continuing on, its being carried on, its being made firm — this is called "resentment".
(2) Contempt and domineering

(a) Therein, what is contempt? The contempt, being contemptuous, the state of contempt, disdain, an act of disdain — this is called "contempt".
(b) Therein, what is domineering? The domineering, being domineering, the taking up of a position for dispute, holding one's own side, refusing to give up — this is called "domineering".
(3) Envy and stinginess

(a) Therein, what is envy? The envy at the gain, honour, respect, esteem, salutation, and veneration of others, the being envious, the state of envy; the jealousy, being jealous, the state of jealousy — this is called "envy".
(b) Therein, what is stinginess? The five kinds of stinginess: stinginess about dwellings, stinginess about families, stinginess about gains, stinginess about praise, stinginess about the teaching. Whatever stinginess of this kind there is, being stingy, the state of stinginess; meanness, miserliness, tight-fistedness, the ungenerous grip of the mind — this is called "stinginess".
(4) Deceit and treachery

(a) Therein, what is deceit? Here someone, having done misconduct with the body, having done misconduct with speech, having done misconduct with the mind, forms an evil wish in order to conceal it. He wishes, "May no one know me"; he intends, "May no one know me"; he speaks words, "May no one know me"; he strives with the body, "May no one know me". Whatever deceit of this kind there is, being deceitful, the going beyond bounds, the cheating, the fraud, the distracting, the evading, the hiding, the concealing, the covering up, the covering over, the not laying open, the not making plain, the keeping covered, the evil act — this is called "deceit".
(b) Therein, what is treachery? Here someone is treacherous, thoroughly treacherous. The treacherousness therein, being treacherous, the state of treachery; the roughness, the crookedness, the studied elegance, the state of studied elegance — this is called "treachery".
(5) Ignorance and craving for existence

(a) Therein, what is ignorance? The lack of knowledge, lack of vision… the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root — this is called "ignorance".
(b) Therein, what is craving for existence? The desire for existence with regard to states of existence, the lust for existence, the delight in existence, the craving for existence, the affection for existence, the burning for existence, the infatuation with existence, the holding fast to existence — this is called "craving for existence".
(6) The view of existence and the view of non-existence

(a) Therein, what is the view of existence? "The self and the world will exist" — whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "the view of existence".
(b) Therein, what is the view of non-existence? "The self and the world will not exist" — whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called the view of non-existence.
(7) The eternalist view and the annihilationist view

(a) Therein, what is the eternalist view? "The self and the world are eternal" — whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "the eternalist view".
(b) Therein, what is the annihilationist view? "The self and the world will be cut off" — whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "the annihilationist view".
(8) The finite view and the infinite view

(a) Therein, what is the view that things are finite? "The self and the world are finite" — whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "the view that things are finite".
(b) Therein, what is the view that things are infinite? "The self and the world are infinite" — whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "the view that things are infinite".
(9) Speculation about the past and about the future

(a) Therein, what is speculation about the past? The view that arises concerning the past, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "speculation about the past".
(b) Therein, what is speculation about the future? The view that arises concerning the future, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "speculation about the future".
(10) Shamelessness and lack of moral dread

(a) Therein, what is shamelessness? Not being ashamed of what one should be ashamed of, not being ashamed of taking up evil, unwholesome things — this is called "shamelessness".
(b) Therein, what is lack of moral dread? Not dreading what one should dread, not dreading taking up evil, unwholesome things — this is called "lack of moral dread".
(11) Being hard to correct and evil friendship

(a) Therein, what is being hard to correct? When one is addressed in accordance with the teaching: the being hard to speak to, the difficulty in correcting, the state of being hard to correct, contrary grasping, delight in opposition, disrespect, disrespectfulness, lack of reverence, lack of deference — this is called "being hard to correct".
(b) Therein, what is evil friendship? Those persons who are without confidence, of bad conduct, of little learning, stingy, and without wisdom — the resorting to them, the frequenting, the close frequenting, the associating with them, the fully associating, the devotion, the full devotion, the being inclined towards them — this is called "evil friendship".
(12) Crookedness and harshness

(a) Therein, what is crookedness? The crookedness, being crooked, the deviousness, the twistedness, the windingness — this is called "crookedness".
(b) Therein, what is harshness? The unpliability, harshness; hardness, roughness, rigidity, stiffness, unyieldingness of mind, unpliability — this is called "harshness".
(13) Impatience and immoderation

(a) Therein, what is impatience? The impatience, being impatient, the not enduring, the fierceness, the rudeness, the mind's dissatisfaction — this is called "impatience".
(b) Therein, what is immoderation? Transgression in body, transgression in speech, transgression in body and speech — this is called "immoderation". All bad conduct is immoderation.
(14) Rough speech and lack of hospitality

(a) Therein, what is rough speech? Whatever speech is prickly, rough, bitter to others, offensive to others, bordering on anger, not conducive to concentration — being a speaker of such speech; the ungentleness of speech therein, the unkindness of speech, the harshness of speech — this is called "rough speech".
(b) Therein, what is lack of hospitality? There are two kinds of hospitality: hospitality with material things and hospitality with the teaching. Here someone shows no hospitality, whether with material things or with the teaching — this is called "lack of hospitality".
(15) Not guarding the doors of the faculties and not knowing moderation in food

(a) Therein, what is not guarding the doors of the faculties? Here someone, having seen a sight with the eye, grasps at its signs and grasps at its details. Since, if he dwelt with the eye faculty unrestrained, covetousness and grief, evil, unwholesome things, might flow in upon him, he does not practise for its restraint, he does not guard the eye faculty, he does not undertake restraint of the eye faculty. Having heard a sound with the ear… having smelled a smell with the nose… having tasted a taste with the tongue… having touched a tangible thing with the body… having known a mental object with the mind, he grasps at its signs and grasps at its details. Since, if he dwelt with the mind faculty unrestrained, covetousness and grief, evil, unwholesome things, might flow in upon him, he does not practise for its restraint, he does not guard the mind faculty, he does not undertake restraint of the mind faculty. The lack of guarding, lack of protection, lack of watching over, lack of restraint of these six faculties — this is called "not guarding the doors of the faculties".
(b) Therein, what is not knowing moderation in food? Here someone takes food without reflection and unwisely — for amusement, for intoxication, for adornment, for beautification. The lack of contentment there, the lack of moderation, the lack of reflection with regard to food — this is called "not knowing moderation in food".
(16) Forgetfulness and lack of clear comprehension

(a) Therein, what is forgetfulness? The absence of mindfulness, absence of recollection, absence of remembering; the absence of mindfulness, the not bearing in mind, the floating away, the forgetting — this is called "forgetfulness".
(b) Therein, what is lack of clear comprehension? The lack of knowledge, lack of vision… the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root — this is called "lack of clear comprehension".
(17) Failure in virtue and failure in view

(a) Therein, what is failure in virtue? Transgression in body, transgression in speech, transgression in body and speech — this is called "failure in virtue". All bad conduct is failure in virtue.
(b) Therein, what is failure in view? "There is nothing given, there is nothing offered… there are in the world no ascetics and brahmins of right conduct and right practice who declare this world and the other world, having realised them for themselves by direct knowledge" — whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "failure in view". All wrong view is failure in view.
(18) The internal fetter and the external fetter

(a) Therein, what is the internal fetter? The five lower fetters are the internal fetter. (b) The five higher fetters are the external fetter.
The Twos.
The Exposition of the Threes
(1) The three unwholesome roots

Therein, what are the three unwholesome roots? Greed, hate, delusion.
(a) Therein, what is greed? The lust, passion, compliance, attraction, delight, delight-and-lust, passion of the mind; wishing, infatuation, holding fast; greed, thorough greed; attachment, the mire, allure, deception; the begetter, the generator, the seamstress, the netter, the river, the clinging vine, the stream, the spreading; the toiler, the companion, the aspiration, what leads on to existence; the forest, the jungle; intimacy, affection, regard, kinship; wishing, the act of wishing, the state of wishing; wishing for sights, wishing for sounds, wishing for smells, wishing for tastes, wishing for tangible things, wishing for gain, wishing for wealth, wishing for children, wishing for life; muttering desire, excessive muttering desire, the act of muttering desire, the state of muttering desire; greediness, being greedy, the state of greediness; itching desire, the wish for what is nice; unrighteous lust, uneven greed; longing, the act of longing, aspiration, envy of what is good, full aspiration; craving for sense pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence, craving for material form, craving for the immaterial, craving for cessation; craving for sounds, craving for sights, craving for smells, craving for tastes, craving for tangible things, craving for mental objects; the flood, the yoke, the tie, the clinging; the obstruction, the hindrance, the covering, the bond; the corruption, the underlying tendency, the obsession; the creeper, the meanness; the root of suffering, the source of suffering, the origin of suffering; Māra's snare, Māra's hook, Māra's range; the river of craving, the net of craving, the leash of craving, the ocean of craving; covetousness, greed, the unwholesome root — this is called "greed".
(b) Therein, what is hate? Resentment arises: "He has done me harm"; resentment arises: "He is doing me harm"; resentment arises: "He will do me harm"; "He has done harm… is doing harm… will do harm to one dear and pleasing to me" — resentment arises; "He has done good… is doing good… will do good to one disliked and displeasing to me" — resentment arises; or resentment arises groundlessly. Whatever resentment of the mind of this kind there is, repugnance, resistance, opposition, anger, being angered, great anger; hate, hating, great hating; the mind's malice, mental hatred; wrath, being wrathful, wrathfulness; hate, hating, state of hating; malice, being malicious, state of being malicious; opposition, hostility, fierceness, rudeness, the mind's dissatisfaction — this is called "hate".
(c) Therein, what is delusion? Not knowing suffering, not knowing the origin of suffering, not knowing the cessation of suffering, not knowing the way leading to the cessation of suffering; not knowing the past, not knowing the future, not knowing the past and the future; not knowing things that are dependently arisen through specific conditionality. Whatever lack of knowledge of this kind there is, lack of vision… the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root — this is called "delusion". These are the three unwholesome roots.
(2) The three unwholesome thoughts

Therein, what are the three unwholesome thoughts? The thought of sense pleasure, the thought of ill will, the thought of cruelty.
(a) Therein, what is the thought of sense pleasure? The thinking, thought, wrong intention connected with sense pleasure — this is called "the thought of sense pleasure".
(b) Therein, what is the thought of ill will? The thinking, thought, wrong intention connected with ill will — this is called "the thought of ill will".
(c) Therein, what is the thought of cruelty? The thinking, thought, wrong intention connected with cruelty — this is called "the thought of cruelty". These are the three unwholesome thoughts.
(3) The three unwholesome perceptions

Therein, what are the three unwholesome perceptions? The perception of sense pleasure, the perception of ill will, the perception of cruelty.
(a) Therein, what is the perception of sense pleasure? The perception, perceiving, state of having perceived connected with sense pleasure — this is called "the perception of sense pleasure".
(b) Therein, what is the perception of ill will? The perception, perceiving, state of having perceived connected with ill will — this is called "the perception of ill will".
(c) Therein, what is the perception of cruelty? The perception, perceiving, state of having perceived connected with cruelty — this is called "the perception of cruelty". These are the three unwholesome perceptions.
(4) The three unwholesome elements

Therein, what are the three unwholesome elements? The element of sense pleasure, the element of ill will, the element of cruelty.
Therein, what is the element of sense pleasure? The thought of sense pleasure is the element of sense pleasure. The thought of ill will is the element of ill will. The thought of cruelty is the element of cruelty.
(a) Therein, what is the thought of sense pleasure? The thinking, thought, wrong intention connected with sense pleasure — this is called "the thought of sense pleasure".
(b) Therein, what is the thought of ill will? The thinking, thought, wrong intention connected with ill will — this is called "the thought of ill will".
(c) Therein, what is the thought of cruelty? The thinking, thought, wrong intention connected with cruelty — this is called "the thought of cruelty". These are the three unwholesome elements.
(5) The three kinds of misconduct

Therein, what are the three kinds of misconduct? Bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct.
(a) Therein, what is bodily misconduct? Killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct — this is called "bodily misconduct".
(b) Therein, what is verbal misconduct? False speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, idle chatter — this is called "verbal misconduct".
(c) Therein, what is mental misconduct? Covetousness, ill will, wrong view — this is called "mental misconduct".
(a–c) Therein, what is bodily misconduct? Unwholesome bodily action is bodily misconduct; unwholesome verbal action is verbal misconduct; unwholesome mental action is mental misconduct.
Therein, what is unwholesome bodily action? Unwholesome bodily intention is unwholesome bodily action; unwholesome verbal intention is unwholesome verbal action; unwholesome mental intention is unwholesome mental action. These are the three kinds of misconduct.
(6) The three mental taints

Therein, what are the three mental taints? The taint of sense pleasure, the taint of existence, the taint of ignorance.
(a) Therein, what is the taint of sense pleasure? The desire for sense pleasures with regard to sense pleasures, the lust for sense pleasures, the delight in sense pleasures, the craving for sense pleasures, the affection for sense pleasures, the burning for sense pleasures, the infatuation with sense pleasures, the holding fast to sense pleasures — this is called "the taint of sense pleasure".
(b) Therein, what is the taint of existence? The desire for existence with regard to states of existence… the holding fast to existence — this is called "the taint of existence".
(c) Therein, what is the taint of ignorance? Not knowing suffering… the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root — this is called "the taint of ignorance". These are the three mental taints.
(7) The three fetters

Therein, what are the three fetters? The view of a self in the body, doubt, wrong grasping of virtue and observances.
(a) Therein, what is the view of a self in the body? Here an unlearned ordinary person — who has no regard for the noble ones, is unskilled in the teaching of the noble ones, untrained in the teaching of the noble ones; who has no regard for good people, is unskilled in the teaching of good people, untrained in the teaching of good people — regards material form as self, or self as possessing material form, or material form as in self, or self as in material form. He regards feeling… perception… formations… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. Whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "the view of a self in the body".
(b) Therein, what is doubt? One doubts and is perplexed about the Teacher; one doubts and is perplexed about the teaching; one doubts and is perplexed about the Order; one doubts and is perplexed about the training; one doubts and is perplexed about the past; one doubts and is perplexed about the future; one doubts and is perplexed about the past and the future; one doubts and is perplexed about things that are dependently arisen through specific conditionality. Whatever doubt of this kind there is, doubting, state of doubting, rigidity of the mind, mental confusion — this is called "doubt".
(c) Therein, what is wrong grasping of virtue and observances? "Purity comes through virtue, purity comes through observances, purity comes through virtue-and-observances of ascetics and brahmins outside this teaching" — whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "wrong grasping of virtue and observances". These are the three fetters.
(8) The three cravings

Therein, what are the three cravings? Craving for sense pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence.
Therein, what is craving for existence? The lust, passion, passion of the mind accompanied by the view of existence — this is called "craving for existence".
Therein, what is craving for non-existence? The lust, passion, passion of the mind accompanied by the annihilationist view — this is called "craving for non-existence". The remaining craving is craving for sense pleasures.
Therein, what is craving for sense pleasures? The lust, passion, passion of the mind connected with the element of sense pleasure — this is called "craving for sense pleasures".
The lust, passion, passion of the mind connected with the element of material form and the element of the immaterial — this is called "craving for existence".
The lust, passion, passion of the mind accompanied by the annihilationist view — this is called "craving for non-existence". These are the three cravings.
(9) Another three cravings

Therein, what are another three cravings? Craving for sense pleasures, craving for material form, craving for the immaterial.
(a) Therein, what is craving for sense pleasures? The lust, passion, passion of the mind connected with the element of sense pleasure — this is called "craving for sense pleasures".
(b) Therein, what is craving for material form? The lust, passion, passion of the mind connected with the element of material form — this is called "craving for material form".
(c) Therein, what is craving for the immaterial? The lust, passion, passion of the mind connected with the element of the immaterial — this is called "craving for the immaterial". These are the three cravings.
(10) Yet another three cravings

Therein, what are yet another three cravings? Craving for material form, craving for the immaterial, craving for cessation.
(a) Therein, what is craving for material form? The lust, passion, passion of the mind connected with the element of material form — this is called "craving for material form".
(b) Therein, what is craving for the immaterial? The lust, passion, passion of the mind connected with the element of the immaterial — this is called "craving for the immaterial".
(c) Therein, what is craving for cessation? The lust, passion, passion of the mind accompanied by the annihilationist view — this is called "craving for cessation". These are the three cravings.
(11) The three quests

Therein, what are the three quests? The quest for sense pleasures, the quest for existence, the quest for a holy life.
(a) Therein, what is the quest for sense pleasures? The desire for sense pleasures with regard to sense pleasures… the holding fast to sense pleasures — this is called "the quest for sense pleasures".
(b) Therein, what is the quest for existence? The desire for existence with regard to states of existence… the holding fast to existence — this is called "the quest for existence".
(c) Therein, what is the quest for a holy life? "The world is eternal", or "the world is not eternal"… or "a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death" — whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "the quest for a holy life".
(a) Therein, what is the quest for sense pleasures? Lust for sense pleasures and the unwholesome bodily action, verbal action, and mental action that stand together with it — this is called "the quest for sense pleasures".
(b) Therein, what is the quest for existence? Lust for existence and the unwholesome bodily action, verbal action, and mental action that stand together with it — this is called "the quest for existence".
(c) Therein, what is the quest for a holy life? The extremist view and the unwholesome bodily action, verbal action, and mental action that stand together with it — this is called "the quest for a holy life". These are the three quests.
(12) The three modes of self-ranking
Therein, what are the three modes of self-ranking? The mode "I am better", the mode "I am equal", the mode "I am worse" — these are the three modes of self-ranking.
(13) The three fears

Therein, what are the three fears? The fear of birth, the fear of aging, the fear of death.
(a) Therein, what is the fear of birth? On account of birth: the fear, fearfulness, terror, horripilation, alarm of mind — this is called "the fear of birth".
(b) Therein, what is the fear of aging? On account of aging: the fear, fearfulness, terror, horripilation, alarm of mind — this is called "the fear of aging".
(c) Therein, what is the fear of death? On account of death: the fear, fearfulness, terror, horripilation, alarm of mind — this is called "the fear of death". These are the three fears.
(14) The three darknesses

Therein, what are the three darknesses? Concerning the past one doubts, is perplexed, does not resolve, does not settle in confidence; concerning the future one doubts, is perplexed, does not resolve, does not settle in confidence; concerning the present one doubts, is perplexed, does not resolve, does not settle in confidence — these are the three darknesses.
(15) The three sectarian grounds

Therein, what are the three sectarian grounds? Here some ascetic or brahmin speaks thus and holds this view: "Whatever this person experiences, whether pleasant or painful or neither painful nor pleasant, all that is caused by what was done in the past." Here some ascetic or brahmin speaks thus and holds this view: "Whatever this person experiences, whether pleasant or painful or neither painful nor pleasant, all that is caused by a supreme being's creation." Here some ascetic or brahmin speaks thus and holds this view: "Whatever this person experiences, whether pleasant or painful or neither painful nor pleasant, all that is without cause and without condition." These are the three sectarian grounds.
(16) The three impediments
Therein, what are the three impediments? Lust is an impediment, hate is an impediment, delusion is an impediment — these are the three impediments.
(17) The three blemishes
Therein, what are the three blemishes? Lust is a blemish, hate is a blemish, delusion is a blemish — these are the three blemishes.
(18) The three stains
Therein, what are the three stains? Lust is a stain, hate is a stain, delusion is a stain — these are the three stains.
(19) The three unevennesses
Therein, what are the three unevennesses? Lust is unevenness, hate is unevenness, delusion is unevenness — these are the three unevennesses.
(20) Another three unevennesses
Therein, what are another three unevennesses? Bodily unevenness, verbal unevenness, mental unevenness — these are the three unevennesses.
(21) The three fires
Therein, what are the three fires? The fire of lust, the fire of hate, the fire of delusion — these are the three fires.
(22) The three corruptions
Therein, what are the three corruptions? The corruption of lust, the corruption of hate, the corruption of delusion — these are the three corruptions.
(23) Another three corruptions
Therein, what are another three corruptions? Bodily corruption, verbal corruption, mental corruption — these are the three corruptions.
(24a) The view of enjoyment

Therein, what is the view of enjoyment? Here some ascetic or brahmin speaks thus and holds this view: "There is no fault in sense pleasures." He plunges into sense pleasures. This is called "the view of enjoyment".
(b) The view of self

Therein, what is the view of self? Here an unlearned ordinary person — who has no regard for the noble ones, is unskilled in the teaching of the noble ones, untrained in the teaching of the noble ones; who has no regard for good people, is unskilled in the teaching of good people, untrained in the teaching of good people — regards material form as self, or self as possessing material form, or material form as in self, or self as in material form. He regards feeling… perception… formations… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. Whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "the view of self".
(c) Wrong view

Therein, what is wrong view? "There is nothing given, there is nothing offered… who declare this world and the other world, having realised them for themselves by direct knowledge" — whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "wrong view". The eternalist view is the view of enjoyment; the view of a self in the body is the view of self; the annihilationist view is wrong view.
(25a) Discontent

Therein, what is discontent? Discontent with remote dwelling places or with any of the higher wholesome things; being discontented, dissatisfaction, not delighting, restlessness, anxiety — this is called "discontent".
(b) Cruelty

Therein, what is cruelty? Here someone harms beings with the hand, or a clod, or a stick, or a knife, or a rope, or with one thing or another; whatever harming of this kind there is, harassing, hurting, injuring, provoking, enraging, doing violence to others — this is called "cruelty".
(c) Unrighteous conduct

Therein, what is unrighteous conduct? Unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct with the body, unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct with speech, unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct with the mind — this is called "unrighteous conduct".
(26a) Being hard to correct

Therein, what is being hard to correct? When one is addressed in accordance with the teaching: the being hard to speak to, the difficulty in correcting, the state of being hard to correct, contrary grasping, delight in opposition, disrespect, disrespectfulness, lack of reverence, lack of deference — this is called "being hard to correct".
(b) Evil friendship

Therein, what is evil friendship? Those persons who are without confidence, of bad conduct, of little learning, stingy, and without wisdom — the resorting to them, the frequenting, the close frequenting, the associating with them, the fully associating, the devotion, the full devotion, the being inclined towards them — this is called "evil friendship".
(c) Perception of diversity

Therein, what is perception of diversity? The perception of sense pleasure, the perception of ill will, the perception of cruelty — this is called "perception of diversity". All unwholesome perception is perception of diversity.
(27a) Restlessness
Therein, what is restlessness? The restlessness of the mind, lack of calm, mental distraction, agitation of the mind — this is called "restlessness".
(b) Laziness

Therein, what is laziness? Letting the mind loose in bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, or the five strands of sense pleasure, and repeatedly letting it loose; acting without respect for the development of wholesome things, acting without perseverance, acting inconstantly, sluggish behaviour, putting down desire, putting down the responsibility, non-practice, non-development, non-cultivation, non-resolution, non-application, heedlessness — this is called "laziness".
(c) Heedlessness

Therein, what is heedlessness? Letting the mind loose in bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, or the five strands of sense pleasure, and repeatedly letting it loose; acting without respect for the development of wholesome things, acting without perseverance, acting inconstantly, sluggish behaviour, putting down desire, putting down the responsibility, non-practice, non-development, non-cultivation, non-resolution, non-application, heedlessness; whatever heedlessness of this kind there is, being heedless, the state of heedlessness — this is called "heedlessness".
(28a) Discontentment

Therein, what is discontentment? The wanting of more by one discontented with whatever robes, alms-food, dwelling place, and medicinal supports for the sick he has, or with the five strands of sense pleasure; whatever desire of this kind there is, being desirous, discontentment, lust, passion, passion of the mind — this is called "discontentment".
(b) Lack of clear comprehension
Therein, what is lack of clear comprehension? The lack of knowledge, lack of vision… the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root — this is called "lack of clear comprehension".
(c) Great desire

Therein, what is great desire? The wanting of more by one discontented with whatever robes, alms-food, dwelling place, and medicinal supports for the sick he has, or with the five strands of sense pleasure; whatever desire of this kind there is, being desirous, great desire, lust, passion, passion of the mind — this is called "great desire".
(29a) Shamelessness
Therein, what is shamelessness? Not being ashamed of what one should be ashamed of, not being ashamed of taking up evil, unwholesome things — this is called "shamelessness".
(b) Lack of moral dread
Therein, what is lack of moral dread? Not dreading what one should dread, not dreading taking up evil, unwholesome things — this is called "lack of moral dread".
(c) Heedlessness

Therein, what is heedlessness? Letting the mind loose in bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, or the five strands of sense pleasure, and repeatedly letting it loose; acting without respect for the development of wholesome things, acting without perseverance, acting inconstantly, sluggish behaviour, putting down desire, putting down the responsibility, non-practice, non-development, non-cultivation, non-resolution, non-application, heedlessness; whatever heedlessness of this kind there is, being heedless, the state of heedlessness — this is called "heedlessness".
(30a) Disrespect

Therein, what is disrespect? The disrespect, disrespectfulness, lack of reverence, lack of deference, lack of regard, absence of regard, the state of having no regard, lack of virtue, lack of consideration — this is called "disrespect".
(b) Being hard to correct

Therein, what is being hard to correct? When one is addressed in accordance with the teaching: the being hard to speak to, the difficulty in correcting, the state of being hard to correct, contrary grasping, delight in opposition, disrespect, disrespectfulness, lack of reverence, lack of deference — this is called "being hard to correct".
(c) Evil friendship

Therein, what is evil friendship? Those persons who are without confidence, of bad conduct, of little learning, stingy, and without wisdom — the resorting to them, the frequenting, the close frequenting, the attending upon them, the associating with them, the fully associating, the devotion, the full devotion, the being inclined towards them — this is called "evil friendship".
(31a) Lack of confidence

Therein, what is lack of confidence? Here someone is without confidence: he does not have confidence in the Buddha, or the teaching, or the Order; whatever lack of confidence of this kind there is, absence of trusting, absence of reliance, absence of full confidence — this is called "lack of confidence".
(b) Uncharitableness

Therein, what is uncharitableness? The five kinds of stinginess: stinginess about dwellings, stinginess about families, stinginess about gains, stinginess about praise, stinginess about the teaching. Whatever stinginess of this kind there is, being stingy, the state of stinginess; meanness, miserliness, tight-fistedness, the ungenerous grip of the mind — this is called "uncharitableness".
(c) Laziness

Therein, what is laziness? Letting the mind loose in bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, or the five strands of sense pleasure, and repeatedly letting it loose; acting without respect for the development of wholesome things, acting without perseverance, acting inconstantly, sluggish behaviour, putting down desire, putting down the responsibility, non-practice, non-development, non-cultivation, non-resolution, non-application, heedlessness — this is called "laziness".
(32a) Restlessness
Therein, what is restlessness? The restlessness of the mind, lack of calm, mental distraction, agitation of the mind — this is called "restlessness".
(b) Non-restraint

Therein, what is non-restraint? Here someone, having seen a sight with the eye, grasps at its signs and grasps at its details. Since, if he dwelt with the eye faculty unrestrained, covetousness and grief, evil, unwholesome things, might flow in upon him, he does not practise for its restraint, he does not guard the eye faculty, he does not undertake restraint of the eye faculty. Having heard a sound with the ear… having smelled a smell with the nose… having tasted a taste with the tongue… having touched a tangible thing with the body… having known a mental object with the mind, he grasps at its signs and grasps at its details. Since, if he dwelt with the mind faculty unrestrained, covetousness and grief, evil, unwholesome things, might flow in upon him, he does not practise for its restraint, he does not guard the mind faculty, he does not undertake restraint of the mind faculty — this is called "non-restraint".
(c) Bad conduct
Therein, what is bad conduct? Transgression in body, transgression in speech, transgression in body and speech — this is called "bad conduct".
(33a) Not wishing to see the noble ones

Therein, what is not wishing to see the noble ones? Therein, who are the noble ones? The Buddhas and the Buddhas' disciples are called the noble ones. The not wishing to see these noble ones, the not wishing to behold them, the not wishing to meet them, the not wishing to come together with them — this is called "not wishing to see the noble ones".
(b) Not wishing to hear the good teaching

Therein, what is not wishing to hear the good teaching? Therein, what is the good teaching? The four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of success, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven awakening factors, the noble eightfold path — this is called "the good teaching". The not wishing to hear this good teaching, the not wishing to listen to it, the not wishing to learn it, the not wishing to retain it — this is called "not wishing to hear the good teaching".
(c) A fault-finding mind

Therein, what is a fault-finding mind? Therein, what is fault-finding? The fault-finding, constant fault-finding, being a fault-finder, constantly finding fault, the state of constant fault-finding, the contempt, the scorn, the disparagement, the seeking of weak points — this is called "a fault-finding mind".
(34a) Forgetfulness

Therein, what is forgetfulness? The absence of mindfulness, absence of recollection, absence of remembering; the absence of mindfulness, the not bearing in mind, the floating away, the forgetting — this is called "forgetfulness".
(b) Lack of clear comprehension
Therein, what is lack of clear comprehension? The lack of knowledge, lack of vision… the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root — this is called "lack of clear comprehension".
(c) Distraction of mind
Therein, what is distraction of mind? The restlessness of the mind, lack of calm, mental distraction, agitation of the mind — this is called "distraction of mind".
(35a) Unwise attention

Therein, what is unwise attention? Unwise attention taking the impermanent as "permanent", unwise attention taking the painful as "pleasant", unwise attention taking what is not self as "self", unwise attention taking the unattractive as "attractive"; or the turning of the mind, repeated turning, engagement, bringing-to-mind, attention contrary to the truth — this is called "unwise attention".
(b) Following the wrong path

Therein, what is following the wrong path? Therein, what is the wrong path? Wrong view, wrong intention, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration — this is called "the wrong path". The resorting to this wrong path, the frequenting, the close frequenting, the associating with it, the fully associating, the devotion, the full devotion, the being inclined towards it — this is called "following the wrong path".
(c) Sluggishness of mind

Therein, what is sluggishness of mind? The mind's lack of readiness, its unworkableness, its sagging, its slumping; sloth, being slothful, the mind's slothfulness; dullness, being dull, the mind's state of dullness — this is called "sluggishness of mind".
The Threes.
The Exposition of the Fours
(1) The four mental taints
Therein, what are the four mental taints? The taint of sense pleasure, the taint of existence, the taint of views, the taint of ignorance.
(a) The taint of sense pleasure

Therein, what is the taint of sense pleasure? The desire for sense pleasures with regard to sense pleasures, the lust for sense pleasures, the delight in sense pleasures, the craving for sense pleasures, the affection for sense pleasures, the burning for sense pleasures, the infatuation with sense pleasures, the holding fast to sense pleasures — this is called "the taint of sense pleasure".
(b) The taint of existence
Therein, what is the taint of existence? The desire for existence with regard to states of existence… the holding fast to existence — this is called "the taint of existence".
(c) The taint of views

Therein, what is the taint of views? "The world is eternal", or "the world is not eternal", or "the world is finite", or "the world is infinite", or "the soul and the body are the same", or "the soul is one thing and the body another", or "a Tathāgata exists after death", or "a Tathāgata does not exist after death", or "a Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death", or "a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death". Whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "the taint of views". All wrong view is the taint of views.
(d) The taint of ignorance

Therein, what is the taint of ignorance? Not knowing suffering, not knowing the origin of suffering, not knowing the cessation of suffering, not knowing the way leading to the cessation of suffering; not knowing the past, not knowing the future, not knowing the past and the future; not knowing things that are dependently arisen through specific conditionality. Whatever lack of knowledge of this kind there is, lack of vision… the barrier of ignorance, delusion, the unwholesome root — this is called "the taint of ignorance". These are the four mental taints.
(2-5) The four ties and the rest

Therein, what are the four ties… the four floods… the four yokes… the four kinds of clinging? Clinging to sense pleasures, clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, clinging to a doctrine of self.
(a) Clinging to sense pleasures
Therein, what is clinging to sense pleasures? The desire for sense pleasures with regard to sense pleasures… the holding fast to sense pleasures — this is called "clinging to sense pleasures".
(b) Clinging to views

Therein, what is clinging to views? "There is nothing given, there is nothing offered… who declare this world and the other world, having realised them for themselves by direct knowledge." Whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "clinging to views". Setting aside clinging to rules and observances and clinging to a doctrine of self, all wrong view is clinging to views.
(c) Clinging to rules and observances

Therein, what is clinging to rules and observances? "Purity comes through virtue, purity comes through observances, purity comes through virtue-and-observances of ascetics and brahmins outside this teaching." Whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "clinging to rules and observances".
(d) Clinging to a doctrine of self

Therein, what is clinging to a doctrine of self? Here an unlearned ordinary person — who has no regard for the noble ones, is unskilled in the teaching of the noble ones, untrained in the teaching of the noble ones; who has no regard for good people, is unskilled in the teaching of good people, untrained in the teaching of good people — regards material form as self, or self as possessing material form, or material form as in self, or self as in material form. He regards feeling… perception… formations… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. Whatever view of this kind there is, resort to views… the distorted grip — this is called "clinging to a doctrine of self". These are the four kinds of clinging.
(6) The four arisings of craving

Therein, what are the four arisings of craving? Craving, when it arises in a monk, arises because of robes; craving, when it arises in a monk, arises because of alms-food; craving, when it arises in a monk, arises because of a dwelling place; craving, when it arises in a monk, arises because of this or that state of being — these are the four arisings of craving.
(7) The four ways of going astray

Therein, what are the four ways of going astray? One goes astray through desire, one goes astray through hate, one goes astray through delusion, one goes astray through fear. Whatever going astray of this kind there is, the wrong course, going by desire, going by faction, going by evasion — these are the four ways of going astray.
(8) The four distortions

Therein, what are the four distortions? Taking the impermanent as "permanent" is a distortion of perception, a distortion of mind, a distortion of view; taking the painful as "pleasant" is a distortion of perception, a distortion of mind, a distortion of view; taking what is not self as "self" is a distortion of perception, a distortion of mind, a distortion of view; taking the unattractive as "attractive" is a distortion of perception, a distortion of mind, a distortion of view — these are the four distortions.
(9) The four ignoble ways of speech

Therein, what are the four ignoble ways of speech? Saying one has seen what one has not seen, saying one has heard what one has not heard, saying one has sensed what one has not sensed, saying one has known what one has not known — these are the four ignoble ways of speech.
(10) Another four ignoble ways of speech

Therein, what are another four ignoble ways of speech? Saying one has not seen what one has seen, saying one has not heard what one has heard, saying one has not sensed what one has sensed, saying one has not known what one has known — these are the four ignoble ways of speech.
(11) The four kinds of misconduct
Therein, what are the four kinds of misconduct? Killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech — these are the four kinds of misconduct.
(12) Another four kinds of misconduct
Therein, what are another four kinds of misconduct? False speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, idle chatter — these are the four kinds of misconduct.
(13) The four fears
Therein, what are the four fears? The fear of birth, the fear of aging, the fear of sickness, the fear of death — these are the four fears.
(14) Another four fears

Therein, what are another four fears? The fear of kings, the fear of thieves, the fear of fire, the fear of water — these are the four fears.
Therein, what are another four fears? The fear of waves, the fear of crocodiles, the fear of whirlpools, the fear of sharks — these are the four fears.
Therein, what are another four fears? The fear of self-reproach, the fear of others' reproach, the fear of punishment, the fear of a bad destination — these are the four fears.
(15) The four views

Therein, what are the four views? The view arises as true and established, "Happiness and suffering are made by oneself"; the view arises as true and established, "Happiness and suffering are made by another"; the view arises as true and established, "Happiness and suffering are made both by oneself and by another"; the view arises as true and established, "Happiness and suffering are made neither by oneself nor by another, but arisen by chance" — these are the four views.
The Fours.
The Exposition of the Fives
(1) The five lower fetters
Therein, what are the five lower fetters? The view of a self in the body, doubt, wrong grasping of virtue and observances, sense desire, ill will — these are the five lower fetters.
(2) The five higher fetters
Therein, what are the five higher fetters? Lust for material form, lust for the immaterial, conceit, restlessness, ignorance — these are the five higher fetters.
(3) The five kinds of stinginess

Therein, what are the five kinds of stinginess? Stinginess about dwellings, stinginess about families, stinginess about gains, stinginess about praise, stinginess about the teaching — these are the five kinds of stinginess.
(4) The five attachments

Therein, what are the five attachments? The attachment of lust, the attachment of hate, the attachment of delusion, the attachment of conceit, the attachment of views — these are the five attachments.
(5) The five darts
Therein, what are the five darts? The dart of lust, the dart of hate, the dart of delusion, the dart of conceit, the dart of views — these are the five darts.
(6) The five barrennesses of mind

Therein, what are the five barrennesses of mind? One doubts and is perplexed about the Teacher, does not resolve, does not settle in confidence; one doubts and is perplexed about the teaching, does not resolve, does not settle in confidence; one doubts and is perplexed about the Order, does not resolve, does not settle in confidence; one doubts and is perplexed about the training, does not resolve, does not settle in confidence; one is angry with one's companions in the holy life, displeased, with a struck-down mind, become barren — these are the five barrennesses of mind.
(7) The five bondages of mind

Therein, what are the five bondages of mind? One is not without lust for sense pleasures, not without desire, not without affection, not without thirst, not without burning, not without craving; one is not without lust for the body… one is not without lust for material form… having eaten as much as one's belly will hold, one dwells devoted to the pleasure of lying down, the pleasure of lolling, the pleasure of sleep; one lives the holy life aspiring to some order of gods — "By this virtue, or observance, or austerity, or holy life, I shall become a god or one among the gods" — these are the five bondages of mind.
(8) The five hindrances

Therein, what are the five hindrances? The hindrance of sense desire, the hindrance of ill will, the hindrance of dullness and drowsiness, the hindrance of restlessness and remorse, the hindrance of doubt — these are the five hindrances.
(9) The five actions with immediate result

Therein, what are the five actions with immediate result? One's mother has been deprived of life, one's father has been deprived of life, an arahant has been deprived of life, the blood of a Tathāgata has been shed with a mind of hatred, the Order has been split — these are the five actions with immediate result.
(10) The five views

Therein, what are the five views? Some declare, "The self is percipient and unimpaired after death"; some declare, "The self is non-percipient and unimpaired after death"; some declare, "The self is neither percipient nor non-percipient and unimpaired after death"; or they proclaim the cutting off, destruction, and non-existence of an existing being; or some declare Nibbāna in this very life — these are the five views.
(11) The five hostilities

Therein, what are the five hostilities? Killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, wine, spirits, and intoxicants that cause heedlessness — these are the five hostilities.
(12) The five losses
Therein, what are the five losses? Loss of relatives, loss of wealth, loss through illness, loss of virtue, loss of view — these are the five losses.
(13) The five dangers of impatience

Therein, what are the five dangers of impatience? One is disliked and displeasing to many people; one has much hostility; one has many faults; one dies confused; with the breakup of the body after death one is reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, hell — these are the five dangers of impatience.
(14) The five fears
Therein, what are the five fears? The fear about livelihood, the fear of disrepute, the fear of timidity in assemblies, the fear of death, the fear of a bad destination — these are the five fears.
(15) The five doctrines of Nibbāna in this very life

Therein, what are the five doctrines of Nibbāna in this very life?
(a) Here some ascetic or brahmin speaks thus and holds this view: "When this self, sir, furnished and provided with the five strands of sense pleasure, amuses itself, to that extent, sir, this self has reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life." Thus some declare the highest Nibbāna in this very life of an existing being.
(b) Another says to him: "There is, sir, that self of which you speak; I do not say it does not exist. But this self, sir, has not to that extent reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life. Why is that? Because, sir, sense pleasures are impermanent, painful, and subject to change; with their change and alteration arise sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. When this self, sir, secluded from sense pleasures… enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption, to that extent, sir, this self has reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life." Thus some declare the highest Nibbāna in this very life of an existing being.
(c) Another says to him: "There is, sir, that self of which you speak; I do not say it does not exist. But this self, sir, has not to that extent reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life. Why is that? Because whatever there is of thought and examination there, by that it is reckoned gross. When this self, sir, with the stilling of thought and examination… enters and dwells in the second meditative absorption, to that extent, sir, this self has reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life." Thus some declare the highest Nibbāna in this very life of an existing being.
(d) Another says to him: "There is, sir, that self of which you speak; I do not say it does not exist. But this self, sir, has not to that extent reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life. Why is that? Because whatever there is of joy and mental elation there, by that it is reckoned gross. When this self, sir, with the fading away of joy… enters and dwells in the third meditative absorption, to that extent, sir, this self has reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life." Thus some declare the highest Nibbāna in this very life of an existing being.
(e) Another says to him: "There is, sir, that self of which you speak; I do not say it does not exist. But this self, sir, has not to that extent reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life. Why is that? Because whatever there is of the mind's engagement with happiness and joy there, by that it is reckoned gross. When this self, sir, with the abandoning of happiness… enters and dwells in the fourth meditative absorption, to that extent, sir, this self has reached the highest Nibbāna in this very life." Thus some declare the highest Nibbāna in this very life of an existing being. These are the five doctrines of Nibbāna in this very life.
The Fives.
The Exposition of the Sixes
(1) The six roots of dispute
Therein, what are the six roots of dispute? Anger, contempt, envy, treachery, evil desire, holding to one's own view — these are the six roots of dispute.
(2) The six desires-and-lusts

Therein, what are the six desires-and-lusts? Desires-and-lusts are things connected with the household life. Household lust for pleasing sights, passion, passion of the mind; for pleasing sounds… for pleasing smells… for pleasing tastes… for pleasing tangible things… household lust for pleasing mental objects, passion, passion of the mind — these are the six desires-and-lusts.
(3) The six grounds of opposition

Therein, what are the six grounds of opposition? Concerning displeasing sights: the resentment of the mind, repugnance, fierceness, rudeness, the mind's dissatisfaction; concerning displeasing sounds… concerning displeasing smells… concerning displeasing tastes… concerning displeasing tangible things… concerning displeasing mental objects: the resentment of the mind, repugnance, fierceness, rudeness, the mind's dissatisfaction — these are the six grounds of opposition.
(4) The six classes of craving

Therein, what are the six classes of craving? Craving for sights, craving for sounds, craving for smells, craving for tastes, craving for tangible things, craving for mental objects — these are the six classes of craving.
(5) The six kinds of disrespect

Therein, what are the six kinds of disrespect? One dwells without respect and without deference for the Teacher; one dwells without respect and without deference for the teaching; one dwells without respect and without deference for the Order; one dwells without respect and without deference for the training; one dwells without respect and without deference for heedfulness; one dwells without respect and without deference for hospitality — these are the six kinds of disrespect.
(6) The six things that lead to decline

Therein, what are the six things that lead to decline? Delight in activity, delight in talk, delight in sleep, delight in company, delight in mingling, delight in proliferation — these are the six things that lead to decline.
(7) Another six things that lead to decline

Therein, what are another six things that lead to decline? Delight in activity, delight in talk, delight in sleep, delight in company, being hard to correct, evil friendship — these are the six things that lead to decline.
(8) The six explorations with joy

Therein, what are the six explorations with joy? Having seen a sight with the eye, one explores a sight that is a basis for joy; having heard a sound with the ear… having smelled a smell with the nose… having tasted a taste with the tongue… having touched a tangible thing with the body… having known a mental object with the mind, one explores a mental object that is a basis for joy — these are the six explorations with joy.
(9) The six explorations with grief

Therein, what are the six explorations with grief? Having seen a sight with the eye, one explores a sight that is a basis for grief; having heard a sound with the ear… having smelled a smell with the nose… having tasted a taste with the tongue… having touched a tangible thing with the body… having known a mental object with the mind, one explores a mental object that is a basis for grief — these are the six explorations with grief.
(10) The six explorations with equanimity

Therein, what are the six explorations with equanimity? Having seen a sight with the eye, one explores a sight that is a basis for equanimity; having heard a sound with the ear… having smelled a smell with the nose… having tasted a taste with the tongue… having touched a tangible thing with the body… having known a mental object with the mind, one explores a mental object that is a basis for equanimity — these are the six explorations with equanimity.
(11) The six kinds of household joy

Therein, what are the six kinds of household joy? Concerning pleasing sights: the mental comfort connected with the household life, the mental happiness, the comfortable happy experience born of mind-contact, the comfortable happy feeling born of mind-contact; concerning pleasing sounds… concerning pleasing smells… concerning pleasing tastes… concerning pleasing tangible things… concerning pleasing mental objects: the mental comfort connected with the household life, the mental happiness, the comfortable happy experience born of mind-contact, the comfortable happy feeling born of mind-contact — these are the six kinds of household joy.
(12) The six kinds of household grief

Therein, what are the six kinds of household grief? Concerning displeasing sights: the mental discomfort connected with the household life, the mental pain, the uncomfortable painful experience born of mind-contact, the uncomfortable painful feeling born of mind-contact; concerning displeasing sounds… concerning displeasing smells… concerning displeasing tastes… concerning displeasing tangible things… concerning displeasing mental objects: the mental discomfort connected with the household life, the mental pain, the uncomfortable painful experience born of mind-contact, the uncomfortable painful feeling born of mind-contact — these are the six kinds of household grief.
(13) The six kinds of household equanimity

Therein, what are the six kinds of household equanimity? Concerning sights that are a basis for equanimity: the mental experience connected with the household life that is neither comfortable nor uncomfortable, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant experience born of mind-contact, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mind-contact; concerning sounds that are a basis for equanimity… concerning smells that are a basis for equanimity… concerning tastes that are a basis for equanimity… concerning tangible things that are a basis for equanimity… concerning mental objects that are a basis for equanimity: the mental experience connected with the household life that is neither comfortable nor uncomfortable, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant experience born of mind-contact, the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling born of mind-contact — these are the six kinds of household equanimity.
(14) The six views

Therein, what are the six views? The view arises in one as true and established, "There is a self for me"; or the view arises in one as true and established, "There is no self for me"; or the view arises in one as true and established, "By self I perceive self"; or the view arises in one as true and established, "By self I perceive non-self"; or the view arises in one as true and established, "By non-self I perceive self"; or else one holds a view like this: "It is this self of mine that speaks and feels, that experiences here and there the result of good and evil actions. It was not born and did not exist before; it was not born and will not exist; it is permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change" — the view arises in one as true and established. These are the six views.
The Sixes.
The Exposition of the Sevens
(1) The seven underlying tendencies

Therein, what are the seven underlying tendencies? The underlying tendency to sensual lust, the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to lust for existence, the underlying tendency to ignorance — these are the seven underlying tendencies.
(2) The seven fetters

Therein, what are the seven fetters? The fetter of sensual lust, the fetter of aversion, the fetter of conceit, the fetter of views, the fetter of doubt, the fetter of lust for existence, the fetter of ignorance — these are the seven fetters.
(3) The seven obsessions

Therein, what are the seven obsessions? The obsession of sensual lust, the obsession of aversion, the obsession of conceit, the obsession of views, the obsession of doubt, the obsession of lust for existence, the obsession of ignorance — these are the seven obsessions.
(4) The seven bad qualities

Therein, what are the seven bad qualities? One is without confidence, one is shameless, one is without moral dread, one is of little learning, one is lazy, one is forgetful, one is without wisdom — these are the seven bad qualities.
(5) The seven kinds of misconduct

Therein, what are the seven kinds of misconduct? Killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, idle chatter — these are the seven kinds of misconduct.
(6) The seven conceits

Therein, what are the seven conceits? Conceit, exaggerated conceit, conceit beyond conceit, self-belittling conceit, over-estimating conceit, the conceit "I am", wrong conceit — these are the seven conceits.
(7) The seven views

(a) Therein, what are the seven views? Here some ascetic or brahmin speaks thus and holds this view: "Since, sir, this self, having material form, made of the four great elements, produced by mother and father, is cut off and destroyed with the breakup of the body and does not exist after death, to that extent, sir, this self is completely cut off." Thus some declare the cutting off, destruction, and non-existence of an existing being.
(b) Another says to him: "There is, sir, that self of which you speak; I do not say it does not exist. But this self, sir, is not to that extent completely cut off.
